title.zh: 卷一百〇三 志第五十一: 刑法二
title.raw: 卷一百〇三 志第五十一: 刑法二 Volume 103 Treatises 56: Punishment and Law 2

sentences.zh: 刑法二 ○職制下

translations.literal: Punishment and Law, Part Two ○ Under Official Regulations
translations.idiomatic: Punishment and Law, Part Two — Official Regulations, Continued

sentences.zh: 諸職官戶在軍籍，管軍官輒追逮其身者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where an official household is on the military register and the commander in charge of troops rashly pursues and arrests the person himself, this is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Where a household registered as official is also enrolled on the military rolls, troop commanders must not pursue and arrest its members in person; this is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸中外大小軍官，不能以法撫循軍人而又害之者，從監察御史廉訪司糾察之；

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers great and small, within and without the capital, fail to comfort and guide soldiers according to law and moreover harm them, the surveillance censors and the surveillance commission shall investigate and prosecute;
translations.idiomatic: Military officers at every level who fail to treat their soldiers lawfully and instead harm them shall be investigated by the censorate and the surveillance commission;

sentences.zh: 行省官及宣慰司元帥府官無故以軍官自衛者，亦如之。

translations.literal: Provincial officials and officials of pacification commissions and marshal's headquarters who without cause employ military officers as personal guards are likewise [subject to investigation].
translations.idiomatic: The same applies to provincial officials and pacification or marshal's headquarters staff who keep military officers as personal guards without proper cause.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官不法，各處憲司就問之，樞府不得委官同問。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers violate the law, the surveillance offices in each place shall question them on the spot; the Bureau of Military Affairs may not delegate officials to join in the questioning.
translations.idiomatic: When military officers break the law, the local surveillance offices shall try them directly; the Bureau of Military Affairs may not send its own officers to sit in on the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 諸管軍官，輒以所佩金銀符充典質者，笞五十七，降散官一等，受質者減二等。

translations.literal: In all cases where commanders in charge of troops rashly use the gold or silver tally they wear as security for a pawn loan, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, are demoted one grade in honorary rank, and the pawnbroker is punished two grades less.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders who pawn the gold or silver tallies they carry receive fifty-seven strokes, lose one honorary rank, and the pawnbroker is punished two grades less severely.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官犯贓，應罷職殿降者，上所佩符，再敘日給之。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers commit bribery and ought to be dismissed and demoted in rank, they surrender the tally they wear; on the day they are reinstated it is given back to them.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers guilty of bribery who are dismissed and demoted must surrender their tallies; the tally is returned when they are reinstated.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官役使軍人，萬戶八名，千戶減萬戶之半，彈壓減千戶之半，過是數者坐罪。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers employ soldiers as servants, a commander of ten thousand households may use eight men, a commander of a thousand households half that of a commander of ten thousand, and a suppression officer half that of a commander of a thousand; exceeding these numbers incurs punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Officers may commandeer soldiers as servants only within fixed limits: eight for a commander of ten thousand households, half that for a thousand-household commander, and half again for a suppression officer; exceeding the quota is punishable.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官驅役軍人，致死非命者，量事斷罪並罷職，征燒埋銀給苦主。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers drive soldiers in forced labor and cause death not by proper sentence, the crime is adjudged according to circumstances and the office is also forfeited; burial compensation silver is levied and given to the bereaved.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who work soldiers to death through forced labor are sentenced according to the circumstances, removed from office, and must pay burial compensation to the victim's family.

sentences.zh: 諸管軍官擅放正軍，及分受雇役錢者，以枉法論，除名不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where commanders in charge of troops rashly release regular soldiers, or share in receiving hire-for-service money, they are judged as bending the law; their names are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders who release regular soldiers without authority, or take a share of hire-for-service payments, are treated as corrupt officials, struck from the roster, and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸管軍官吏克除軍人衣糧鹽菜錢，並全未給散，會赦，克除已招者追給，未招者免征，未給散者給散。

translations.literal: In all cases where commanders and clerks in charge of troops deduct soldiers' clothing, grain, and salt-and-vegetable money, or fail to distribute it entirely, when an amnesty occurs: for deductions already confessed, restitution is pursued; for those not confessed, collection is waived; for amounts not distributed, distribution is ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and clerks who skim soldiers' clothing, grain, or salt allowances, or fail to pay them out, are treated as follows at amnesty: confessed deductions must be repaid, unconfessed ones are forgiven, and unpaid balances must be disbursed.

sentences.zh: 其私役軍人官牛，帶種官地，並管民官占種官地，所收子粒，已招者追沒，未招者免征。

translations.literal: As for privately employing soldiers or official oxen, sowing official land, and civilian officials occupying and sowing official land: the grain harvested—if confessed, it is pursued and confiscated; if not confessed, collection is waived.
translations.idiomatic: Where they privately use soldiers or official oxen, sow official land, or where civilian officials occupy and farm official land, harvested grain from confessed offenses is confiscated; unconfessed cases are waived.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官役其出征軍人家屬，又借之錢而多取息者，並坐之。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers employ the families of soldiers on campaign, or lend them money and take excessive interest, all are punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who commandeer the families of soldiers on campaign, or lend them money at usurious rates, are all liable to punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官輒縱軍人誣民以罪，嚇取錢物而分贓自厚者，計贓科罪，除名不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers rashly allow soldiers to falsely charge commoners with crimes, intimidate them into yielding money and goods, and divide the spoils to enrich themselves, the bribe is calculated for sentencing, the name is struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who let soldiers frame civilians, extort money and goods, and keep a share of the loot are sentenced by the amount stolen, struck from the roster, and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸民間失火，鎮守軍官坐視不救，而反縱軍剽掠者，從臺憲官糾之。

translations.literal: In all cases where commoners suffer fire, garrison commanders sit by and do not rescue them but instead allow soldiers to plunder, the censorate and surveillance officials shall investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When fire breaks out among the people, garrison commanders who fail to help and instead let soldiers loot shall be investigated by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官輒斷民訟者，禁之，違者罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers rashly adjudicate civil lawsuits, this is prohibited; violators are punished.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers must not hear civil suits; violators are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官挾仇犯分，輒持刃欲殺連帥者，杖六十七，解職別敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers harbor a grudge and overstep their station, rashly taking up a blade intending to kill their commanding general, they receive sixty-seven strokes of the staff, are removed from office and reassigned elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who, bearing a private grudge, draw weapons intending to kill their commander receive sixty-seven strokes, lose their post, and may serve only in another assignment.

sentences.zh: 諸投下官吏受贓，與常選官同論。

translations.literal: In all cases where appanage officials accept bribes, they are judged the same as regularly selected officials.
translations.idiomatic: Appanage officials who take bribes are punished on the same terms as regularly appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 諸投下雜職犯贓罪者罷之，不以常調殿降論。

translations.literal: In all cases where appanage miscellaneous subordinates commit bribery, they are dismissed and are not judged by the rules for demotion in rank of regular appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous appanage staff guilty of bribery are simply dismissed, without the demotion schedule applied to regular officials.

sentences.zh: 諸投下妄稱上旨，影占民站，除其徭役，故縱為民害者，杖七十七，沒其家財之半，所占民杖一百七，還元籍。

translations.literal: In all cases where appanage holders falsely claim the imperial will, covertly seize commoners' relay stations, exempt them from corvée, and deliberately allow harm to the people, they receive seventy-seven strokes of the staff; half their household property is confiscated; the commoners seized receive one hundred seven strokes and are returned to their original registers.
translations.idiomatic: Appanage holders who falsely claim imperial authority, seize relay stations and exempt their occupants from corvée to the people's harm receive seventy-seven strokes and forfeit half their property; the seized commoners receive one hundred seven strokes and are restored to their original registers.

sentences.zh: 諸王傅文卷，監察御史考閱，與有司同。

translations.literal: In all cases of princely tutors' documents and dossiers, surveillance censors examine them, the same as regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: The dossiers of princely tutors are reviewed by surveillance censors on the same terms as those of regular offices.

sentences.zh: 諸位下置財賦營田等司，歲終則會；

translations.literal: In all cases where appanages establish offices for revenue, farming colonies, and the like, at year's end there is a reckoning;
translations.idiomatic: Appanages that maintain revenue and farming-colony offices must hold a year-end reckoning;

sentences.zh: 會畢，從廉訪司考閱之。

translations.literal: when the reckoning is finished, the surveillance commission examines it.
translations.idiomatic: after which the surveillance commission reviews the accounts.

sentences.zh: 諸投下輕重囚徒，並從廉訪司審錄。

translations.literal: In all cases of appanage prisoners light and heavy, all are examined and recorded by the surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: All appanage prisoners, whether for minor or serious offenses, are tried and recorded by the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 諸藩邸事務，大者奏裁，小者移中書，擅以教令行者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of princely residence affairs, great matters are memorialized for imperial decision, small matters are referred to the Secretariat; rashly issuing instructional orders is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Princely household affairs of major import go to the throne for decision and minor ones to the Secretariat; princes may not issue orders on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 諸倉庾官吏與府州司縣官吏人等，以百姓合納稅糧，通同攬納，接受折價飛鈔者，十石以上，各刺面，杖一百七；

translations.literal: In all cases where granary officials and prefectural, district, and county officials and the like, taking the tax grain commoners ought to pay, collude to contract collection and accept discounted flying notes, for ten piculs or more each is tattooed on the face and beaten one hundred seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: Granary officials and local magistrates who collude to collect tax grain in kind but accept discounted paper notes instead—for ten piculs or more—are tattooed and beaten one hundred seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 十石以下，九十七；

translations.literal: for less than ten piculs, ninety-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: for less than ten piculs, ninety-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 官吏除名不敘。

translations.literal: officials are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: the officials are struck from the roster and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 退閑官吏、豪勢富戶、行鋪人等違犯者，十石之上，杖九十七；

translations.literal: Retired officials, powerful wealthy households, shopkeepers, and the like who violate: for ten piculs or more, ninety-seven strokes of the staff;
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials, powerful households, and shopkeepers who violate the rule receive ninety-seven strokes for ten piculs or more;

sentences.zh: 十石之下，八十七。

translations.literal: for less than ten piculs, eighty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: and eighty-seven strokes for less than ten piculs.

sentences.zh: 其部糧官吏知情分受，五十七，除名不敘。

translations.literal: Grain-distribution officials who knowingly share in receipt receive fifty-seven strokes and are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Grain officials who knowingly take a share receive fifty-seven strokes and are struck from the roster without reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 有失覺察者，監臨部糧官吏，二十七；

translations.literal: Those who fail to detect it: supervising grain-distribution officials, twenty-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising grain officials who fail to detect the offense receive twenty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 府州總部糧官吏，一十七。

translations.literal: prefectural chief grain-distribution officials, seventeen strokes.
translations.idiomatic: and prefectural chief grain officials seventeen strokes.

sentences.zh: 若能捕獲犯人者，與免本罪。

translations.literal: If they can capture the offenders, they are granted exemption from the original offense.
translations.idiomatic: Those who capture the offenders are exempted from punishment for the original offense.

sentences.zh: 若倉官人吏等盜糶官糧，與攬納飛鈔同論。

translations.literal: If granary officials and clerks and the like steal and sell official grain, they are judged the same as contracting collection and flying notes.
translations.idiomatic: Granary officials who steal and sell government grain are punished on the same terms as those who take flying notes for tax grain.

sentences.zh: 知情糴買，十石以上，杖一百七；

translations.literal: Those who knowingly purchase: for ten piculs or more, one hundred seven strokes of the staff;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing purchasers of ten piculs or more receive one hundred seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 十石之下，九十七。

translations.literal: for less than ten piculs, ninety-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: and ninety-seven strokes for less than ten piculs.

sentences.zh: 其漕運官吏有失覺察者，驗糧數多寡治罪。

translations.literal: Transport officials who fail to detect it are punished according to the amount of grain involved.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-transport officials who fail to detect the offense are punished according to the quantity of grain involved.

sentences.zh: 其盜糶糧價，結攬飛鈔，追征沒官，正糧於倉官，並結攬糴買人均征還官。

translations.literal: The price of stolen and sold grain and contracted flying notes are pursued, levied, and confiscated for the state; the proper grain is charged to the granary official, and contractors and purchasers alike are levied to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Proceeds from stolen grain and illicit notes are seized for the state; granary officials must make up the proper grain, and contractors and buyers must repay the government in full.

sentences.zh: 諸倉庫官吏人等盜所主守錢糧，一貫以下，決五十七，至十貫杖六十七，每二十貫加一等；

translations.literal: In all cases where warehouse officials and the like steal money and grain they are charged to guard: for one string or less, fifty-seven strokes are imposed; up to ten strings, sixty-seven strokes of the staff; for every twenty strings one degree is added;
translations.idiomatic: Warehouse officials who steal money or grain in their charge receive fifty-seven strokes for one string or less, sixty-seven up to ten strings, and one additional degree of punishment for every twenty strings;

sentences.zh: 一百二十貫，徒一年，每三十貫加半年；

translations.literal: one hundred twenty strings, penal servitude one year; for every thirty strings half a year is added;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred twenty strings brings one year of penal servitude, with half a year added for every thirty strings;

sentences.zh: 二百四十貫，徒三年；

translations.literal: two hundred forty strings, penal servitude three years;
translations.idiomatic: two hundred forty strings brings three years of penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 三百貫處死。

translations.literal: three hundred strings, death.
translations.idiomatic: and three hundred strings is punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 計贓以至元鈔為則，諸物以當時價估折計之。

translations.literal: In calculating the bribe, Zhiyuan notes are the standard; all goods are estimated and converted at the current price.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes are calculated in Zhiyuan paper notes, with other goods converted at current prices.

sentences.zh: 諸倉庫官、知庫子、攢典、鬥腳人等，侵盜移易官物，匿不舉發者，與犯人同罪；

translations.literal: In all cases where warehouse officials, warehouse managers, registry clerks, porters, and the like embezzle, steal, or transfer official goods and conceal without reporting, they share the offender's crime;
translations.idiomatic: Warehouse officials, managers, clerks, and porters who embezzle or transfer government goods and fail to report it share the offender's punishment;

sentences.zh: 失覺察者，減犯人罪四等。

translations.literal: Those who fail to detect it have the offender's crime reduced by four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fail to detect it are punished four degrees less severely than the offender.

sentences.zh: 諸倉庫錢糧出納，所設首領官及提舉監支納以下攢典合幹人以上，互相覺察，若有違法短少，一體均陪，任內收支錢糧，正收倒除皆完，方許給由。

translations.literal: In all cases of warehouse money and grain receipts and disbursements, the chief officials established, the supervisors of receipt and disbursement, and registry clerks and combined clerks and above shall mutually watch one another; if there is illegal shortage, all share liability equally; within their term of office, receipts and disbursements of money and grain must be fully collected and fully accounted, and only then may a certificate of clearance be issued.
translations.idiomatic: For warehouse receipts and disbursements, chief officials, supervisors, and clerks must watch one another; any illegal shortage is shared equally; clearance certificates are issued only when all money and grain for the term is fully accounted.

sentences.zh: 諸典守鈔庫官，已倒昏鈔，不用退印，笞五十七，解見任。

translations.literal: In all cases where note-vault custodian officials have already exchanged worn notes but fail to use the return seal, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod and are removed from their current post.
translations.idiomatic: Note-vault custodians who exchange worn notes without applying the return seal receive fifty-seven strokes and are removed from office.

sentences.zh: 提調官失計點，笞一十七，並記過名。

translations.literal: Supervising officials who fail to count receive seventeen strokes of the rod and a demerit is recorded in their dossier.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising officials who fail to inspect receive seventeen strokes and a demerit on their record.

sentences.zh: 諸鈔庫官，輒以自己昏鈔詭名倒換者，笞三十七，記過。

translations.literal: In all cases where note-vault officials rashly use their own worn notes under a false name to exchange, they receive thirty-seven strokes of the rod and a demerit is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Note-vault officials who exchange their own worn notes under false names receive thirty-seven strokes and a demerit.

sentences.zh: 諸平準行用庫倒換昏鈔，多取工墨錢，庫官知而不曾分贓者，減一等，並解職別敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where stabilization and circulation vaults exchange worn notes and take excessive processing fees, vault officials who knew but did not share in the bribe have punishment reduced one degree and are removed from office for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Stabilization vaults that exchange worn notes for excessive fees are punished; officials who knew but took no share receive one degree less punishment and are reassigned.

sentences.zh: 主謀又受贓者，以枉法論，除名不敘。

translations.literal: Ringleaders who also accept bribes are judged as bending the law; their names are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Ringleaders who also take bribes are treated as corrupt officials, struck from the roster, and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸白紙坊典守官，私受桑楮皮折價者，計贓以枉法論，除名不敘，仍追贓，收買本色還官。

translations.literal: In all cases where paper-mill custodian officials privately accept discounted payment for mulberry-bark pulp, the bribe is calculated and they are judged as bending the law; their names are struck from the roster with no reinstatement; the bribe is still pursued, the goods in kind are purchased and returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Paper-mill custodians who take private payment for pulp at a discount are sentenced for bribery, struck from the roster, and must repay the state in kind.

sentences.zh: 諸京倉受糧，部官董之，外倉收糧，州縣長官董之。

translations.literal: In all cases of capital granaries receiving grain, ministry officials supervise; for outer granaries receiving grain, prefectural and county chiefs supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Capital granaries are supervised by ministry officials; provincial granaries by prefectural and county chiefs.

sentences.zh: 收不如法致腐敗者，按治官通究之。

translations.literal: If collection is not according to law and causes spoilage, the investigating officials pursue all responsible parties.
translations.idiomatic: If grain is received improperly and spoils, all responsible officials are investigated.

sentences.zh: 諸倉官委任親屬為家丁，致盜糶官糧者，笞五十七，解職殿敘；

translations.literal: In all cases where granary officials appoint relatives as household retainers, leading to theft and sale of official grain, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod and are removed from office with demotion in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Granary officials who appoint relatives as retainers, leading to theft and sale of government grain, receive fifty-seven strokes and are demoted;

sentences.zh: 同僚相容隱，四十七，解職。

translations.literal: colleagues who tolerate and conceal it receive forty-seven strokes and are removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: colleagues who conceal the offense receive forty-seven strokes and lose their posts.

sentences.zh: 諸倉官輒翻釘官斛，多收民租，主謀者笞五十七，同僚初不知情，既知而不能改正者，三十七，並解職別敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where granary officials rashly alter and re-nail official measuring vessels to over-collect civilian rent, ringleaders receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod; colleagues who at first did not know but once knowing cannot correct it receive thirty-seven strokes; all are removed from office for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Granary officials who tamper with official measures to overcharge rent: ringleaders receive fifty-seven strokes; colleagues who learn of it but fail to stop it receive thirty-seven; all are reassigned.

sentences.zh: 諸京師每日散糶官米，人止一斗，權豪勢要及有祿之家，輒糴買者，笞二十七，追中統鈔二十五貫，付告人充賞。

translations.literal: In all cases where the capital daily sells official rice, each person is limited to one peck; powerful families and salaried households who rashly buy receive twenty-seven strokes of the rod; twenty-five strings of Zhongtong notes are pursued and given to the informant as reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital's daily rice sales each person may buy only one peck; powerful or salaried households who buy more receive twenty-seven strokes, and twenty-five strings of Zhongtong notes are paid to the informant.

sentences.zh: 諸官局造作典守，輒克除材料者，計贓以枉法論，除名不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where government workshop custodians rashly deduct materials, the amount is calculated for sentencing as bending the law; their names are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Workshop custodians who skim materials are sentenced for bribery, struck from the roster, and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸運司辦課官，取受事發，辦課畢日追問；

translations.literal: In all cases where transport-office tax-collection officials are found to have accepted bribes, they are questioned on the day tax collection is completed;
translations.idiomatic: Transport-office tax officials found taking bribes are questioned once collection for the period is finished;

sentences.zh: 受代離職者，就問之。

translations.literal: those who have been replaced and left office are questioned where they are.
translations.idiomatic: those who have already left office are questioned in their current location.

sentences.zh: 諸鹽場官勘問人致死者，從轉運司差官攝其職，發犯人歸有司。

translations.literal: In all cases where salt-field officials examine and question persons to death, the transport office dispatches an official to act in their place and sends the offender to the regular authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-field officials whose interrogations cause death are replaced by transport-office appointees, and the offender is handed to the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 諸稅務官，輒以民到務文契，枉作匿稅，私其罰錢者，以枉法論，除名不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where tax-office officials rashly take civilians' documents on arrival at the office, falsely treat them as tax evasion, and keep the fines privately, they are judged as bending the law; their names are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Tax officials who falsely declare valid documents to be tax evasion and keep the fines are treated as corrupt, struck from the roster, and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸財賦總管淘金提舉司存，雖有護持制書，事應糾劾者，監察御史廉訪司準法行之。

translations.literal: In all cases of revenue general administrations, gold-washing offices, and the like, even if they hold protective imperial documents, where matters ought to be impeached, surveillance censors and the surveillance commission shall proceed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue administrations and gold offices, even when holding protective edicts, may still be impeached by the censorate and surveillance commission as the law provides.

sentences.zh: 諸守庫藏軍官，夜不直宿，致有盜者，笞三十七，還職。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers guarding treasuries fail to stand night watch, leading to theft, they receive thirty-seven strokes of the rod and return to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers guarding treasuries who fail to stand night watch, allowing theft, receive thirty-seven strokes and return to duty.

sentences.zh: 捕盜不獲者，圍宿軍官軍人追陪所失物貨，俟獲盜征贓給還。

translations.literal: If thieves are not captured, the encamped military officers and soldiers must make restitution for the goods lost; when the thief is captured, the stolen goods are levied and returned.
translations.idiomatic: If thieves are not caught, the garrison officers and soldiers must compensate for the loss; when the thief is caught, stolen goods are recovered and returned.

sentences.zh: 若遇強劫，軍官軍人力所不及者，不在追斷之限。

translations.literal: If they encounter armed robbery beyond the officers' and soldiers' power to prevent, they are not within the limit of pursuit and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: They are not liable when armed robbery occurs beyond their power to prevent.

sentences.zh: 諸雜造局院，輒與諸人帶造軍器者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where miscellaneous manufacturing bureaus rashly allow various persons to bring in and manufacture weapons, this is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous manufacturing bureaus may not allow private persons to bring in and make weapons; this is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸兩浙財賦府隸徽政者，掌治錢谷造作，歲終報成，以次年正月至於二月，從廉訪司稽其文書，違者糾之。

translations.literal: In all cases of the Two Zhe revenue office subordinate to the Huizheng Office, which manages money, grain, and manufacturing: at year's end they report completion; from the first to the second month of the following year the surveillance commission audits their documents; violators are investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Zhe revenue office under Huizheng reports at year-end; from the first to the second month of the next year the surveillance commission audits its accounts and investigates violations.

sentences.zh: 諸有司橋梁不修，道途不治，雖修治而不牢強者，按治及監臨官究治之。

translations.literal: In all cases where responsible offices fail to repair bridges or maintain roads, or repair them but not solidly, the investigating officials and supervising officials pursue all responsible parties.
translations.idiomatic: Offices that fail to maintain bridges and roads, or do so inadequately, are investigated together with their supervisors.

sentences.zh: 諸有司不以時修築堤防，霖雨既降，水潦並至，漂民廬舍，溺民妻子，為民害者，本郡官吏各罰俸一月，縣官各笞二十七，典史各一十七，並記過名。

translations.literal: In all cases where responsible offices fail to repair dikes in season, and after heavy rains floodwaters arrive together, sweeping away commoners' houses and drowning wives and children, harming the people: prefectural officials each forfeit one month's salary; county officials each receive twenty-seven strokes of the rod; clerks each seventeen strokes; demerits are recorded in all dossiers.
translations.idiomatic: Offices that fail to maintain dikes on time, so that floods destroy homes and drown people: prefectural officials forfeit one month's salary, county officials receive twenty-seven strokes, clerks seventeen, and all receive demerits.

sentences.zh: 諸漕運官，輒拘括水陸舟車，阻滯商旅者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where grain-transport officials rashly seize water and land boats and carts, obstructing merchants and travelers, this is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-transport officials may not seize boats and carts and obstruct merchants and travelers; this is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸漕運官，輒受贓，縱水手人等以稻糠盜換官糧者，以枉法計贓論罪，除名不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where grain-transport officials rashly accept bribes and allow sailors and the like to steal and substitute chaff for official grain, they are sentenced by calculating the bribe as bending the law; their names are struck from the roster with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Transport officials who take bribes and let sailors substitute chaff for government grain are sentenced for corruption, struck from the roster, and barred from reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸海道都漕運萬戶府所轄千戶已下有罪，萬戶問之；

translations.literal: In all cases where commanders of a thousand households and below under the Maritime Route Grand Grain-Transport Ten-Thousand-Household Office commit offenses, the commander of ten thousand households questions them;
translations.idiomatic: Officers of a thousand households and below under the maritime grain-transport command are tried by the ten-thousand-household commander;

sentences.zh: 萬戶有罪，行省問之。

translations.literal: if the commander of ten thousand households is guilty, the provincial administration questions him.
translations.idiomatic: the provincial administration tries the ten-thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 徇情者，監察御史廉訪司察之，漕事畢，然後廉訪司考其案牘。

translations.literal: Those who show favoritism are investigated by surveillance censors and the surveillance commission; when transport duties are finished, the surveillance commission then examines their case files.
translations.idiomatic: Favoritism is investigated by the censorate; after transport duties end, the surveillance commission reviews the case files.

sentences.zh: 諸海道運糧船戶，盜糶官糧，詐稱遭風覆沒者，計贓刺斷，雖會赦，仍刺之。

translations.literal: In all cases where maritime grain-transport boat households steal and sell official grain and falsely claim it was lost in wind and sinking, the bribe is calculated, they are tattooed and sentenced; even if an amnesty occurs, they are still tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Maritime grain carriers who steal government grain and claim shipwreck are sentenced by the amount stolen and tattooed; tattooing stands even at amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣行李，脫脫禾孫及驛吏輒敢搜檢者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys' baggage is searched by tuotuohesun attendants or relay clerks who rashly dare to inspect it, this is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys' baggage may not be searched by attendants or relay clerks; this is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣行橐過重，壓損驛馬，而脫脫禾孫與使臣交贈為好，不以法稱盤者，笞二十七，記過。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys' traveling packs are excessively heavy, injuring relay horses, and tuotuohesun attendants exchange gifts with envoys on friendly terms and fail to weigh by regulation, they receive twenty-seven strokes of the rod and a demerit is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants who fail to weigh envoys' overweight baggage, injuring relay horses, because they are on friendly terms with the envoy receive twenty-seven strokes and a demerit.

sentences.zh: 諸急遞鋪，輒開所遞實封文書，妄入無名文字者，笞五十七。

translations.literal: In all cases where express relay stations rashly open sealed documents in transit and insert unauthorized text, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Express relay stations that open sealed documents in transit or add unauthorized text receive fifty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 諸急遞鋪，每上下半月，府州判官縣主簿親臨檢視，所遞文字但有稽違、磨擦、沈匿，鋪司鋪兵即驗事重輕論罪，各路正官一員總之，廉訪司察之。

translations.literal: In all cases of express relay stations, every first and second half of the month the prefectural judge and county registrar personally inspect; for documents in transit that show delay, tampering, or concealment, relay managers and couriers are immediately sentenced according to the gravity of the matter; one chief official in each circuit oversees this; the surveillance commission investigates.
translations.idiomatic: Express relay stations are inspected twice monthly by prefectural judges and county registrars; delays, tampering, or concealment of documents are punished according to severity; one circuit chief oversees each route, and the surveillance commission investigates.

sentences.zh: 其有弗職，親臨官初犯笞一十七，再犯加一等，三犯呈省別議，總提調官減親臨官一等。

translations.literal: If they neglect duty, inspecting officials on first offense receive seventeen strokes of the rod; on second offense one degree is added; on third offense it is reported to the province for separate deliberation; the overall supervising official is punished one degree less than the inspecting official.
translations.idiomatic: Neglect of duty: inspecting officials receive seventeen strokes on first offense, more on second, and third offenses go to the province; the overall supervisor is punished one degree less.

sentences.zh: 每季具申上司，有無稽違，仍於各官任滿日，解由開寫，而黜陟之。

translations.literal: Each quarter a full report is submitted to superiors on whether there were delays; moreover, on the day each official's term ends, the certificate of clearance states this, and promotion or demotion follows.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter superiors receive reports on delays; officials' clearance certificates at term's end record this for promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣輒騎懷駒馬者，取與各笞五十七，及以車易馬者，俱坐之。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys rashly ride pregnant mares, giver and receiver each receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod; those who exchange a cart for a horse are all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys who ride pregnant mares: both parties receive fifty-seven strokes; those who trade a cart for a horse are likewise punished.

sentences.zh: 諸公主下嫁，迎送往還，並不得由傳置。

translations.literal: In all cases of princesses marrying down, welcoming and sending parties going and returning may not use the relay system.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses' wedding parties may not use the official relay system for travel.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣在城，輒騎占驛馬者禁之，違者罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys in the city rashly ride and seize relay horses, this is prohibited; violators are punished.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys in the capital may not seize relay horses for private use; violators are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸驛使在道，奪回馬易所乘馬，馳至死者，償其直。

translations.literal: In all cases where relay couriers on the road seize another's horse and exchange it for the horse they ride, and ride it to death, they compensate its value.
translations.idiomatic: Relay couriers who seize another's horse, exchange it for their mount, and ride it to death must pay its value.

sentences.zh: 若以私事故選良馬馳至死者，笞二十七，仍償其直。

translations.literal: If for private affairs they select a good horse and ride it to death, they receive twenty-seven strokes of the rod and still compensate its value.
translations.idiomatic: Couriers who pick a good horse for private business and ride it to death receive twenty-seven strokes and must still pay its value.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣多取分例，笞一十七，追所多還官，記過。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys take excessive per-diem allowances, they receive seventeen strokes of the rod; the excess is pursued and returned to the state; a demerit is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys who take excessive per-diem allowances receive seventeen strokes, must return the excess, and receive a demerit.

sentences.zh: 使還人員，除軍情急務外，日不過三驛，驛官仍於關文標寫起止程期，違者各笞二十七，再犯罷役。

translations.literal: Returning envoys and personnel, except for urgent military affairs, may not exceed three relay stations per day; relay officials still mark start, end, and schedule on the pass document; violators each receive twenty-seven strokes of the rod; on second offense they are dismissed from service.
translations.idiomatic: Returning envoys may travel no more than three relay stations per day except for urgent military business; relay officials record schedules on passes; violators receive twenty-seven strokes, and repeat offenders are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸乘驛使臣，或枉道營私，橫索祗待，或訪舊逸遊，餓損馬乘，並申聞斷治。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys using relays deviate from the route for private profit, demand hospitality by force, visit old acquaintances for idle travel, or starve and injure horses and mounts—all are reported and sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys who detour for private gain, extort hospitality, travel idly to visit friends, or neglect and harm relay horses are reported and punished.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣枉道馳驛者，笞五十七；

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys deviate from the route and rush the relays, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod;
translations.idiomatic: Envoys who detour while using the relays receive fifty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 脫脫禾孫擅依隨給驛者，依例科罰。

translations.literal: tuotuohesun attendants who on their own authority follow along and obtain relays are punished according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: attendants who improperly obtain relay service are punished according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 諸驛使詐改公牒，多起馬者，杖八十七；

translations.literal: In all cases where relay couriers fraudulently alter official documents to obtain extra horses, they receive eighty-seven strokes of the staff;
translations.idiomatic: Relay couriers who falsify documents to obtain extra horses receive eighty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 其部押官馬，輒夾帶私馬，多取草料者，並沒入其私馬。

translations.literal: those who escort official horses and rashly bring private horses along to take extra fodder—all have their private horses confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: escorts who bring private horses to draw extra fodder have their private horses confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸朝廷軍情大事，奉旨遣使者，佩以金字圓符給驛，其餘小事，止用御寶聖旨。

translations.literal: In all cases of major military affairs of the court, envoys dispatched by imperial edict wear gold-character round tallies to obtain relays; for other minor matters, only imperial-seal edicts are used.
translations.idiomatic: For major military affairs the court dispatches envoys with gold round tallies for relay service; minor matters require only imperial-seal edicts.

sentences.zh: 諸王公主駙馬亦為軍情急務遣使者，佩以銀字圓符給驛，其餘止用御寶聖旨。

translations.literal: Princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law who also dispatch envoys for urgent military affairs wear silver-character round tallies to obtain relays; for the rest, only imperial-seal edicts are used.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law dispatching envoys for urgent military affairs use silver round tallies for relays; other business requires imperial-seal edicts only.

sentences.zh: 若濫給者，從臺憲官糾察之。

translations.literal: If relays are given abusively, the censorate and surveillance officials shall investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Abusive grant of relay service is investigated by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 諸高麗使臣，所帶徒從，來則俱來，去則俱去，輒留中路郡邑買賣者，禁之；

translations.literal: In all cases of Goryeo envoys, the attendants they bring must all come together and all leave together; rashly leaving them behind in intermediate prefectures and districts to trade is prohibited;
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo envoys' attendants must travel together on arrival and departure; leaving them behind en route to trade is forbidden;

sentences.zh: 易馬出界者，禁之。

translations.literal: Those who barter horses and take them beyond the border—prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Bartering horses and exporting them across the frontier is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸出使官員，所至輒受官吏筵宴，及官吏輒相邀請，並從風憲糾察。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys wherever they arrive rashly accept banquets from local officials, and officials rashly invite one another—all are prosecuted under surveillance discipline.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where traveling envoys accept banquets from local officials, or officials press such invitations on one another, the surveillance officials shall investigate and prosecute.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣所過州縣，無故不得入城。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys pass through prefectures and counties, they may not enter the city without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys passing through prefectures and counties may not enter city walls without good reason.

sentences.zh: 有故入城者，止於公館安宿，輒宿於官民之家者，從風憲糾之。

translations.literal: Where there is cause to enter the city, they lodge only in the public hostel; those who rashly lodge in officials' or commoners' houses are prosecuted under surveillance discipline.
translations.idiomatic: If they must enter a city, they shall lodge only at the official hostel; lodging in private homes—official or common—is subject to surveillance discipline.

sentences.zh: 諸遣使開讀詔書，所過州郡就便開讀者聽，非所經由而輒往者禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys are dispatched to proclaim and read imperial edicts, they are permitted to read at convenience in prefectures and commanderies they pass through; those who rashly go to places not on their route are prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys commissioned to proclaim edicts may read them at convenience in jurisdictions they pass through; going elsewhere without being routed there is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 若本宗事須親往者，不在此限。

translations.literal: If the matter of their own mission requires going in person, this limit does not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Where the business of the mission itself requires a personal visit, this restriction does not apply.

sentences.zh: 諸使臣所至之處，有親戚故舊，禮應追往者聽。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys reach a place and have relatives or old friends whom ritual propriety requires them to visit, this is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys may visit relatives or old friends when etiquette requires, in places they pass through.

sentences.zh: 諸受命出使還，匿給驛文字符節及錫貢之物，久不進者，杖六十七，記過。

translations.literal: In all cases where those who return from missions conceal relay documents, tallies, and bestowed tribute goods and long fail to present them, they receive sixty-seven strokes of the staff and a demerit is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys who conceal relay passes, credentials, or gifts received on mission and long delay surrendering them receive sixty-seven strokes of the staff and a recorded demerit.

sentences.zh: 諸進表使臣，五日外不還職，托故稽留，他有營者，止所給驛，籍其姓名，罷黜之。

translations.literal: In all cases where memorial-presenting envoys beyond five days do not return to office, use pretexts to delay, or pursue other business, relay provision is stopped, their names are registered, and they are dismissed and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial envoys who fail to resume office after five days, linger on pretext, or pursue private affairs shall lose relay support, have their names recorded, and be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 諸出使郡國，使事之外，毋有所與，有必須上聞者，實封以聞。

translations.literal: In all cases where envoys go to commanderies and states, beyond mission business they may have no involvement; matters that must be reported upward are sealed in substance and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to provinces must confine themselves strictly to mission business; anything that must reach the throne shall be reported in a sealed dispatch.

sentences.zh: 諸銜命出使，輒將有司刑囚審斷者，罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where those bearing imperial orders on mission rashly take judicial prisoners under the relevant office and adjudicate them, they are punished.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where envoys bearing imperial orders independently try and sentence prisoners under the jurisdiction of local authorities, they are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸奉使循行郡縣，有告廉訪司官不法者，若其人嘗為風憲所黜罷，則與監察御史雜問之，余聽專問。

translations.literal: In all cases where commissioners touring commanderies and counties receive reports of unlawful conduct by surveillance commission officials, if the person was once dismissed by surveillance discipline, they are questioned jointly with surveillance censors; otherwise they may question exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners investigating reports against surveillance commission officials shall question jointly with surveillance censors if the accused was previously dismissed by the surveillance offices; otherwise the commissioner may question alone.

sentences.zh: 諸官吏公差，輒受人贐行禮物者，隨事論罪，官還職，吏發鄰道貼補。

translations.literal: In all cases where officials and clerks on public assignment rashly accept farewell gifts and traveling presents, guilt is adjudged according to the matter; officials return to office, clerks are dispatched to neighboring circuits for supplementary service.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and clerks on public business who accept bribes or farewell gifts are punished according to the offense; officials may return to office, while clerks are reassigned to neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜，境內若失過盜賊，卻獲他境盜賊，許令功過相補。

translations.literal: In all cases of bandit-catching, if within the jurisdiction bandits are lost but bandits from another jurisdiction are captured, merit and fault may offset each other.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catchers lose thieves within their jurisdiction but capture thieves from another jurisdiction, merit and fault may offset each other.

sentences.zh: 如獲他境強盜，或偽造寶鈔二起，各準境內強盜一起，無強者準竊盜二起。

translations.literal: If strong bandits from another jurisdiction are captured, or two cases of counterfeiting treasure notes are made, each counts as one strong-bandit case within the jurisdiction; where there are no strong bandits, each counts as two theft cases.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing strong bandits or two cases of forged treasure notes from another jurisdiction each counts as one local strong-bandit case; where no strong bandits exist locally, each counts as two theft cases.

sentences.zh: 如獲竊盜，準亦如之。

translations.literal: If thieves are captured, the standard is likewise applied.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing thieves from another jurisdiction follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 如境內無失，但獲強竊盜賊，依例理賞。

translations.literal: If within the jurisdiction there is no loss but strong or petty bandits are captured, rewards are granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Where no local loss has occurred but strong or petty thieves are captured, rewards are granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 若應捕之人，及事主等告指捕獲者，不賞。

translations.literal: If those who ought to catch them, or victims and the like who identify and capture them, no reward is given.
translations.idiomatic: No reward is given when the capture is made by persons obligated to pursue thieves or by victims who identified the offenders.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜官，不得差遣，違者臺憲官糾之。

translations.literal: In all cases, bandit-catching officials may not be reassigned for dispatch; violators are prosecuted by censorate officials.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catching officials are reassigned for other duties, the censorate shall investigate and prosecute.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜官，任內失過盜賊，除獲別境盜準折外，三限不獲，強盜三起，竊盜五起，各笞一十七；

translations.literal: In all cases where bandit-catching officials within their term lose bandits, apart from offsetting with captures from other jurisdictions, if within three periods they fail to capture three strong-bandit cases or five theft cases, each receives seventeen strokes of the rod;
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catching officials lose thieves during their term, beyond offsetting with out-of-jurisdiction captures, failure within three periods to catch three strong-bandit or five theft cases brings seventeen strokes of the rod each;

sentences.zh: 強盜五起，竊盜十起，各笞二十七；

translations.literal: five strong-bandit cases and ten theft cases—each receives twenty-seven strokes of the rod;
translations.idiomatic: five strong-bandit or ten theft cases uncaught brings twenty-seven strokes of the rod each;

sentences.zh: 強盜十起，竊盜十五起，各笞三十七。

translations.literal: ten strong-bandit cases and fifteen theft cases—each receives thirty-seven strokes of the rod.
translations.idiomatic: ten strong-bandit or fifteen theft cases uncaught brings thirty-seven strokes of the rod each.

sentences.zh: 鎮守軍官一體捕限者同罪，親民提控捕盜官，減罪二等。

translations.literal: Garrison commanders who share the same arrest quotas are guilty of the same crime; civil officials supervising bandit-catching officials have their guilt reduced two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison officers subject to the same arrest quotas face the same penalties; civil officials supervising bandit-catchers receive punishment two grades lighter.

sentences.zh: 其限內獲賊及半者免罪，若諸人獲盜應賞者，賞之。

translations.literal: If within the period bandits are captured to half the quota, guilt is waived; if others capture bandits eligible for reward, they are rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing half the lost bandits within the period absolves guilt; where the public captures bandits eligible for reward, rewards are still granted.

sentences.zh: 諸南北兵馬司，職在巡警非違，捕逐盜賊，輒理民訟者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where the northern and southern military patrol commissioners, whose duty is to patrol for irregularities and pursue bandits, rashly adjudicate civil lawsuits, this is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where the northern and southern military patrol commissioners, whose duty is patrol and bandit pursuit, handle civil lawsuits instead, this is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸南北兵馬司，罪囚八十七以下，決遣；

translations.literal: In all cases where the northern and southern military patrol commissioners, for criminal prisoners below eighty-seven strokes, adjudicate and dispatch;
translations.idiomatic: The northern and southern military patrol commissioners may directly adjudicate and dispose of crimes punishable by fewer than eighty-seven strokes of the rod;

sentences.zh: 應刺配者，就刺配之。

translations.literal: those requiring tattooing and banishment are tattooed and banished on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: those requiring tattooing and exile are tattooed and exiled where they are held.

sentences.zh: 諸各路在城錄事錄判，分番巡捕，若有失盜，止坐巡捕官。

translations.literal: In all cases where in each circuit the urban recorders and assistant recorders take turns in patrol and arrest, if bandits are lost only the patrol officers bear guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In all circuits, urban recorders and assistants take rotating patrol shifts; if theft occurs, only the patrol officers bear responsibility.

sentences.zh: 諸職官非應捕之人，告獲反賊者，升二等用。

translations.literal: In all cases where officials who are not persons obliged to catch bandits report and capture rebels, they are employed two grades higher.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials not obligated to catch bandits report and capture rebels, they receive promotion two grades higher.

sentences.zh: 諸告獲強盜，每名官給賞錢至元鈔五十貫，竊盜二十五貫，新獲者倍之，獲強盜至五人與一官。

translations.literal: In all cases where strong bandits are reported and captured, for each person the state gives reward money of fifty strings of Zhiyuan notes, for thieves twenty-five strings; for newly captured persons it is doubled; capturing strong bandits up to five persons grants one office.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where strong bandits are reported and captured, the state awards fifty strings of Zhiyuan notes per person, twenty-five for thieves, doubled for fresh captures; capturing five strong bandits grants an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 諸捕獲弒逆凶徒，比獲強盜給賞。

translations.literal: In all cases where parricide and treasonous murderers are captured, rewards are given as for capturing strong bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where parricide and treasonous murderers are captured, rewards match those for strong bandits.

sentences.zh: 諸隨處鎮守軍官軍人，親獲強竊盜賊者，減半給賞。

translations.literal: In all cases where garrison officers and soldiers everywhere personally capture strong or petty bandits, half the reward is given.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where garrison officers and soldiers personally capture strong or petty bandits, they receive half the standard reward.

sentences.zh: 諸都城失盜，一年不獲者，勒巡軍陪償所盜財物，其敢差占巡軍者禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where in the capital bandits are lost and not captured within one year, patrol soldiers are compelled to compensate the stolen property; those who dare reassign patrol soldiers are prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where theft in the capital goes unsolved for a year, patrol soldiers must compensate the stolen goods; unauthorized reassignment of patrol soldiers is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜官捕獲強竊盜賊，不即牒發，淹禁死亡者，杖七十七，罷職。

translations.literal: In all cases where bandit-catching officials capture strong or petty bandits but do not immediately dispatch them by memorandum, and prolonged detention causes death, they receive seventy-seven strokes of the staff and are dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catching officials delay dispatching captured bandits and prolonged detention causes death, they receive seventy-seven strokes of the staff and are removed from office.

sentences.zh: 諸盜牛馬，悔過放還者，以竊盜已行不得財論，不征倍贓賞錢；

translations.literal: In all cases where cattle and horses are stolen and the thief repents and returns them, it is adjudged as theft attempted but property not obtained; double-restitution reward money is not levied;
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where cattle thieves repent and return the animals, the offense is treated as attempted theft without gain, and double-restitution reward money is not levied;

sentences.zh: 有司輒以常盜刺斷者，以刑名違錯科罰。

translations.literal: if the relevant office rashly applies ordinary theft sentencing and tattooing, they are punished for error in penal nomenclature.
translations.idiomatic: officials who apply ordinary theft sentencing to such cases are punished for incorrect application of penal law.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜官，輒受人遞至匿名文字，枉勘平人為盜，致囚死獄中者，杖九十七，罷職不敘；

translations.literal: In all cases where bandit-catching officials rashly accept anonymously delivered writings handed on by others, wrongfully examine commoners as bandits, and cause prisoners to die in jail, they receive ninety-seven strokes of the staff, are dismissed from office with no reinstatement;
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catching officials accept anonymous denunciations, wrongfully convict innocents as bandits, and cause death in prison, they receive ninety-seven strokes of the staff and permanent dismissal;

sentences.zh: 正問官六十七，降先職二等敘；

translations.literal: the presiding interrogator receives sixty-seven strokes, is reassigned two grades below former rank;
translations.idiomatic: the presiding interrogator receives sixty-seven strokes and is reassigned two grades below his former rank;

sentences.zh: 首領官笞四十七，註邊遠一任；

translations.literal: the supervisory official receives forty-seven strokes of the rod, with notation for one remote appointment;
translations.idiomatic: the supervisory official receives forty-seven strokes of the rod and a notation for one remote appointment;

sentences.zh: 承吏杖六十七，罷役不敘；

translations.literal: the handling clerk receives sixty-seven strokes of the staff, is dismissed from service with no reinstatement;
translations.idiomatic: the handling clerk receives sixty-seven strokes of the staff and dismissal from service without reinstatement;

sentences.zh: 主意寫匿名文書者，杖一百七，流遠；

translations.literal: the instigator who wrote the anonymous document receives one hundred seven strokes of the staff and exile to the far frontier;
translations.idiomatic: the author of the anonymous document receives one hundred seven strokes of the staff and exile to the far frontier;

sentences.zh: 遞送匿名文書者，減二等；

translations.literal: those who handed on the anonymous document have guilt reduced two grades;
translations.idiomatic: those who delivered the anonymous document receive punishment two grades lighter;

sentences.zh: 受命主事遞送者，減三等。

translations.literal: those who received orders and handled the delivery have guilt reduced three grades.
translations.idiomatic: those who were commanded to deliver it receive punishment three grades lighter.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜官搜捕逆賊，輒將平人審問蹤跡，乘怒毆之，邂逅致死者，杖六十七，解職別敘，記過，征燒埋銀給苦主。

translations.literal: In all cases where bandit-catching officials search for rebels, rashly take commoners and interrogate their tracks, beat them in anger, and accidentally cause death, they receive sixty-seven strokes of the staff, are removed from office and reassigned elsewhere, a demerit is recorded, and burial compensation silver is levied for the bereaved.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catching officials beat innocent people during rebel searches in anger and accidentally cause death, they receive sixty-seven strokes of the staff, removal with reassignment elsewhere, a recorded demerit, and burial compensation levied for the victim.

sentences.zh: 諸捕盜官受財故縱賊囚者，與犯人同罪，已敗獲者，徒杖並減一等。

translations.literal: In all cases where bandit-catching officials accept bribes and deliberately release bandit prisoners, they share the prisoner's crime; if already captured in defeat, exile and staff punishments are each reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where bandit-catching officials take bribes to release prisoners, they share the prisoner's crime, reduced one grade if the prisoner was already captured.

sentences.zh: 諸父有罪，不坐其子；

translations.literal: In all cases where the father has guilt, the son is not implicated;
translations.idiomatic: A father's guilt does not extend to his son;

sentences.zh: 兄有罪，不坐其弟。

translations.literal: where the elder brother has guilt, the younger brother is not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: an elder brother's guilt does not extend to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 諸大宗正府理斷人命重事，必以漢字立案牘，以公文稱憲臺，然後監察御史審覆之。

translations.literal: In all cases where the Grand Council of the Imperial Clan adjudicates capital cases involving human life, they must establish case documents in Chinese characters, address the censorate in official documents, and only then do surveillance censors review them.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where the Imperial Clan Council adjudicates capital cases, it must record them in Chinese characters, address the censorate in official documents, and then await review by surveillance censors.

sentences.zh: 諸有司非法用刑者，重罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices use punishment unlawfully, they are heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials employ illegal torture, they face severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 已殺之人，輒臠割其肉而去者禁之，違者重罪之。

translations.literal: Those who rashly dismember the flesh of persons already executed and take it away are prohibited; violators are heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: Dismembering the corpses of executed persons to take flesh is forbidden; violators face severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸鞫獄不能正其心，和其氣，感之以誠，動之以情，推之以理，輒施以大披掛及王侍郎繩索，並法外慘酷之刑者，悉禁止之。

translations.literal: In all cases where in interrogating prisoners they cannot rectify the heart and harmonize the qi, move them with sincerity, stir them with feeling, and deduce with reason, but rashly apply the great hanging rack and Vice Minister Wang's rope, together with cruel punishments outside the law—all are prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In all interrogation, officials who fail to proceed with sincerity and reason but instead apply cruel extralegal torture such as the great hanging rack and Vice Minister Wang's rope—all such methods are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸鞫問罪囚，除朝省委問大獄外，不得寅夜問事，廉訪司察之。

translations.literal: In all cases of interrogating criminal prisoners, apart from major cases commissioned for interrogation by the court, they may not examine matters at dawn or night; the surveillance commission inspects this.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal interrogation, except for major cases commissioned by the court, may not be conducted at dawn or night; the surveillance commission shall oversee compliance.

sentences.zh: 諸各路推官專掌推鞫刑獄，平反冤滯，董理州縣刑名之事，其餘庶務，毋有所與，按治官歲錄其殿最，秩滿則上其事而黜陟之。

translations.literal: In all cases the judicial reviewers of each circuit exclusively manage interrogation of criminal prisoners, redress wrongful detentions, supervise prefectural and county penal matters; in other miscellaneous affairs they may have no involvement; investigating officials annually record their grades of achievement, and when their term ends they report the matter for promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit judicial reviewers shall exclusively handle criminal interrogation, redress wrongful detentions, and supervise county sentencing; they may not involve themselves in other duties; investigating officials record annual performance, and at term's end report for promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 凡推官若受差不聞上司，輒離職者，亦坐罪。

translations.literal: As for judicial reviewers, if on receiving assignment they do not inform their superiors and rashly leave their post, they also bear guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial reviewers who leave their posts on assignment without notifying superiors are likewise punished.

sentences.zh: 諸處斷重囚，雖叛逆，必令臺憲審錄，而後斬於市曹。

translations.literal: In all cases where capital prisoners are sentenced locally, even for treason, the censorate must review and record them, and only then are they beheaded at the execution ground.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where capital sentences are imposed locally, even for treason, the censorate must review the case before execution at the market.

sentences.zh: 諸內外囚禁，從各路正官及監察御史廉訪司以時審錄，輕者斷遣，重者結案，其有冤滯，就糾察之。

translations.literal: In all cases of imprisonment within and without, following each circuit's chief administrator and surveillance censors and the surveillance commission, they review and record in season; the light are sentenced and dispatched, the heavy have cases concluded; where there is wrongful detention, it is investigated on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: All prisoners within and without the capital shall be periodically reviewed by circuit administrators and surveillance officials; light sentences are disposed, heavy cases concluded, and unjust detentions investigated on the spot.

sentences.zh: 諸正蒙古人，除犯死罪，監禁依常法，有司毋得拷掠，仍日給飲食。

translations.literal: In all cases of pure Mongols, apart from capital crimes, imprisonment follows the regular law; the relevant offices may not torture, and daily food and drink are still provided.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Mongols, except for capital crimes, are imprisoned under regular law without torture, with daily food provided.

sentences.zh: 犯真奸盜者，解束帶佩囊，散收。

translations.literal: Those guilty of true adultery or theft have belt and purse removed and are held loosely.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of adultery or theft have belts and purses removed and are held under loose guard.

sentences.zh: 余犯輕重者，以理對證，有司勿執拘之，逃逸者監收。

translations.literal: For remaining offenses light or heavy, they are confronted according to reason; the relevant offices must not forcibly detain them; those who flee are imprisoned and held.
translations.idiomatic: For other offenses light or heavy, they are tried on their merits without forced detention; absconders are imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 諸奏決天下囚，值上怒，勿輒奏。

translations.literal: In all cases of memorializing decisions on prisoners throughout the realm, when the sovereign is angry, do not rashly memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: When reporting capital sentences to the throne during imperial anger, officials shall not immediately memorialize.

sentences.zh: 上欲有所誅，必遲回一二日，乃覆奏。

translations.literal: If the sovereign wishes to execute someone, one must delay one or two days and then resubmit the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign wishes to execute someone, officials must wait one or two days before resubmitting the memorial.

sentences.zh: 諸有司因公依理決罰，邂逅身死者，不坐。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices on public business lawfully impose punishment according to reason and accidentally cause death, they are not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials lawfully punish on public business and accidentally cause death, they are not liable.

sentences.zh: 諸累過不悛，年七十以上，應罰贖者，仍減等科決。

translations.literal: In all cases of repeated offenses without reform, for those over seventy who ought to pay fines in commutation, they still receive reduced-grade physical punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat offenders over seventy who should pay fines in commutation still receive reduced-grade physical punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸犯罪，二罪俱發，以重者論，罪等從一。

translations.literal: In all cases of crime, when two crimes are discovered together, the heavier is applied in judgment; where crimes are equal, one is followed.
translations.idiomatic: When two crimes are discovered together, the heavier governs; where crimes are equal, they are treated as one.

sentences.zh: 若一罪先發，已經論決，余罪後發，其輕若等，勿論；

translations.literal: If one crime is discovered first and has already been adjudged, and remaining crimes are discovered later, if they are lighter or equal, no further action;
translations.idiomatic: If a lighter or equal crime was already decided and a later crime of equal or lesser weight arises, no further action is taken;

sentences.zh: 重者，更論之，通計前罪，以充後數。

translations.literal: if heavier, they are adjudged again, counting the prior crime in total to satisfy the later count.
translations.idiomatic: if heavier, the case is retried, counting the prior conviction toward the later sentence.

sentences.zh: 諸職官輒以微故，乘怒不取招詞，斷決人邂逅致死，又誘苦主焚瘞其屍者，笞五十七，解職別敘，記過。

translations.literal: In all cases where officials rashly on a slight pretext, taking advantage of anger, do not obtain confession, sentence persons and accidentally cause death, and moreover induce the bereaved to burn and bury the corpse, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, are removed from office and reassigned elsewhere, and a demerit is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials rashly sentence without obtaining testimony in anger, accidentally cause death, and induce the bereaved to burn the body, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, removal with reassignment elsewhere, and a recorded demerit.

sentences.zh: 諸鞫獄輒以私怨暴怒，去衣鞭背者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where in interrogating prisoners they rashly act from private grudge in violent anger, strip clothing and whip the back—prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Stripping prisoners and whipping their backs in private anger during interrogation is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸鞫問囚徒，重事須加拷訊者，長貳僚佐會議立案，然後行之，違者重加其罪。

translations.literal: In all cases of interrogating criminal prisoners, for serious matters requiring added torture, the chief and deputy with colleagues confer, establish a case record, and only then carry it out; violators have their guilt heavily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Torture in serious cases requires joint planning and filing by senior officials before execution; violators face aggravated punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸弓兵祗候獄卒，輒毆死罪囚者，為首杖一百七，為從減一等，均征燒埋銀給苦主，其枉死應徵倍贓者，免征。

translations.literal: In all cases where bow soldiers, attendants, or jailers rashly beat capital prisoners to death, the principal receives one hundred seven strokes of the staff, accomplices have guilt reduced one grade, burial compensation silver is levied equally for the bereaved; where wrongful death should levy double restitution, it is not levied.
translations.idiomatic: Bow soldiers, attendants, or jailers who beat capital prisoners to death receive one hundred seven strokes as principals, accomplices one grade less, with burial compensation levied for victims; wrongful-death double restitution is waived.

sentences.zh: 諸有司輒收禁無罪之人者，正官並笞一十七，記過。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices rashly imprison and detain persons without guilt, the chief administrator together receives seventeen strokes of the rod and a demerit is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials imprison the innocent, the chief administrator receives seventeen strokes of the rod and a recorded demerit.

sentences.zh: 無招枉禁，致自縊而死者，笞三十七，期年後敘。

translations.literal: Wrongful imprisonment without confession, causing suicide by hanging, brings thirty-seven strokes of the rod and reinstatement after one year.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongful imprisonment without confession leading to suicide by hanging brings thirty-seven strokes of the rod and reinstatement after one year.

sentences.zh: 諸有司輒將無辜枉禁，瘐死者，解職，降先品一等敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices rashly wrongfully imprison the innocent and they die from neglect in detention, they are removed from office and reassigned one grade below former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials wrongfully imprison the innocent and they die from neglect in detention, the official is removed and reassigned one grade below former rank.

sentences.zh: 諸有司承告被盜，輒將警跡人，非理枉勘身死，卻獲正賊者，正問官笞五十七，解職，期年後，降先職一等敘；

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices receive reports of theft, rashly take trace witnesses, unlawfully examine them to death, yet later capture the true bandit, the presiding interrogator receives fifty-seven strokes of the rod, is removed from office, and after one year is reassigned one grade below former rank;
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials receiving theft reports wrongfully torture trace witnesses to death but later capture the real thief, the presiding interrogator receives fifty-seven strokes of the rod, removal, and reassignment one grade below former rank after one year;

sentences.zh: 首領官及承吏，各五十七，罷役不敘；

translations.literal: the supervisory official and handling clerk each receive fifty-seven strokes, are dismissed from service with no reinstatement;
translations.idiomatic: the supervisory official and handling clerk each receive fifty-seven strokes and dismissal from service without reinstatement;

sentences.zh: 均征燒埋銀給苦主，通記過名。

translations.literal: burial compensation silver is levied equally for the bereaved, and demerits are recorded for all.
translations.idiomatic: burial compensation is levied for the victim, with demerits recorded for all involved.

sentences.zh: 諸有司受財故縱正賊，誣執非罪，非法拷訊，連逮妻子，銜冤赴獄，事未曉白，身已就死，正官杖一百七，除名，佐官八十七，降二等雜職敘，仍均征燒埋銀。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices accept bribes and deliberately release the true bandit, falsely seize the innocent, unlawfully torture, detain wives and children together, and the wronged go to prison bearing grievance—before the matter is clarified the person is already dead—the chief administrator receives one hundred seven strokes of the staff and is struck from the roster, the assistant eighty-seven strokes and reassignment two grades lower in miscellaneous posts, and burial compensation silver is still levied equally.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials take bribes to release real thieves while framing innocents with illegal torture, detaining their families, and causing death before the case is clarified, the chief receives one hundred seven strokes and removal, assistants eighty-seven strokes with two-grade demotion to miscellaneous posts, and burial compensation is levied jointly.

sentences.zh: 諸有司故入人罪，若未決者及囚自死者，以所入罪減一等論，入人全罪，以全罪論，若未決放，仍以減等論。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices knowingly impose guilt on persons, if not yet decided or the prisoner dies by suicide, the imposed crime is reduced one grade in judgment; imposing the full crime on a person is judged by the full crime; if released before decision, reduced-grade judgment still applies.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials knowingly impose guilt, if the person is uncondemned or dies by suicide before judgment, punishment is reduced one grade from the imposed crime; imposing full guilt draws full guilt; if released before judgment, reduced-grade punishment still applies.

sentences.zh: 諸故出人之罪，應全科而未決放者，從減等論，仍記過。

translations.literal: In all cases of knowingly releasing a person's guilt, where the full crime ought to apply but release occurs before decision, reduced-grade judgment is followed and a demerit is still recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials knowingly release guilty persons who should receive full punishment before judgment, reduced-grade punishment applies and a demerit is recorded.

sentences.zh: 諸失入人之罪者，減三等，失出人罪者減五等，未決放者又減一等，並記過。

translations.literal: In all cases of erroneous imposition of guilt, guilt is reduced three grades; erroneous release of guilt is reduced five grades; if released before decision, one more grade is reduced; demerits are recorded in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: Erroneous imposition of guilt is reduced three grades; erroneous release five grades; if released before judgment, one further grade is reduced; a demerit is recorded in each case.

sentences.zh: 諸有司失出人死罪者，笞五十七，解職，期年後降先品一等敘，記過，正犯人追禁結案。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices erroneously release persons from capital crimes, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, are removed from office, after one year are reassigned one grade below former rank, a demerit is recorded, and the actual offender is pursued, imprisoned, and the case concluded.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials erroneously release persons from capital crimes, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, removal, reassignment one grade below former rank after one year, a recorded demerit, and the actual offender is rearrested and the case concluded.

sentences.zh: 諸有司輒將革前雜犯，承問斷遣者，以故入論。

translations.literal: In all cases where the relevant offices rashly take miscellaneous offenses from before the reform and adjudicate and dispatch them on inquiry, it is judged as knowing imposition of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials apply pre-reform miscellaneous offenses to sentencing, it is treated as knowing false imposition of guilt.

sentences.zh: 諸監臨挾仇，違法枉斷所監臨職官者，抵罪不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where supervisors harbor grudges and unlawfully judge wrongly the officials they supervise, they suffer equivalent guilt with no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where supervisors illegally judge subordinates from personal grudges, they suffer equivalent guilt without reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸審囚官強愎自用，輒將蒙古人刺字者，杖七十七，除名，將已刺字去之。

translations.literal: In all cases where trial officials are obstinate and self-willed, rashly tattooing Mongols, they receive seventy-seven strokes of the staff, are struck from the roster, and existing tattoos are removed.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where trial officials obstinately tattoo Mongols in violation of law, they receive seventy-seven strokes of the staff, removal from the roster, and any tattoos applied are removed.

sentences.zh: 諸為盜，並從有司歸問，各投下輒擅斷遣者，坐罪。

translations.literal: In all cases of theft, all are returned for questioning to the relevant offices; appanage lords who rashly adjudicate and dispatch on their own bear guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases of theft, jurisdiction belongs to the proper authorities; appanage lords who adjudicate on their own are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸鬥毆殺人，無輕重，並結案上省部詳讞。

translations.literal: In all cases of fighting and beating causing death, regardless of severity, cases are concluded and sent up to the provincial ministry for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases of fighting resulting in death, regardless of severity, cases must be concluded and submitted to the provincial ministry for review.

sentences.zh: 有司輒任情擅斷者，笞五十七，解職，其年後，降先品一等敘。

translations.literal: If the relevant offices rashly follow their own inclination and adjudicate on their own authority, they receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, are removed from office, and in that year thereafter are reassigned one grade below former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who arbitrarily decide such cases receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod, removal from office, and reassignment one grade below former rank within the year.

sentences.zh: 諸禁囚因械梏不嚴，致反獄者，直日押獄杖九十七，獄卒各七十七，司獄及提牢官皆坐罪，百日內全獲者不坐。

translations.literal: In all cases where imprisoned persons because fetters are not strict break prison, the day-duty jail guard receives ninety-seven strokes of the staff, each jail soldier seventy-seven, the prison warden and chief jail officer all bear guilt; if all are recaptured within one hundred days, they are not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where prisoners break jail because restraints were lax, the day-duty guard receives ninety-seven strokes of the staff, each jailer seventy-seven, and wardens are punished; if all escapees are recaptured within one hundred days, no guilt attaches.

sentences.zh: 諸罪在大惡，官吏受贓縱令私和者，罷之。

translations.literal: In all cases where crimes are among the great evils and officials accept bribes and permit private settlement, they are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where officials take bribes to permit private settlement of crimes among the greatest evils, they are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸司獲受財，縱犯奸囚人，在禁疏枷飲酒者，以枉法科罪，除名。

translations.literal: In all cases where prison wardens accept property, permit adultery prisoners in loose cangue to drink wine in detention, they are sentenced for bending the law and struck from the roster.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where jailers take bribes to allow adultery prisoners loose shackles and wine in detention, they are punished for bending the law and removed from the roster.

sentences.zh: 諸流囚，強盜持杖不曾傷人，但得財，若得財至二十貫，為從；

translations.literal: In all cases of exiled prisoners, strong bandits wielding staves who have not injured persons but obtained property—if property obtained reaches twenty strings, they are accomplices;
translations.idiomatic: Among crimes punishable by exile, armed robbers who have not injured anyone but took property count as accomplices if the haul reaches twenty strings;

sentences.zh: 不持仗，不曾傷人，得財四十貫，為從；

translations.literal: not wielding staves, not having injured persons, property obtained forty strings—they are accomplices;
translations.idiomatic: unarmed robbers who have not injured anyone but took forty strings count as accomplices;

sentences.zh: 及竊盜，割車剜房，傷事主，為從；

translations.literal: and thieves who cut carts and gouge rooms, injuring the victim, are accomplices;
translations.idiomatic: burglars who break into carts or rooms and injure victims count as accomplices;

sentences.zh: 不曾傷事主，但曾得財；
