translations.literal: not having injured the victim but having obtained property;
translations.idiomatic: those who did not injure the victim but took property;

sentences.zh: 不曾得財，內有舊賊；

translations.literal: not having obtained property, among them being old thieves;
translations.idiomatic: those who took no property but include repeat thieves;

sentences.zh: 初犯怯烈司盜駝馬牛，為從；

translations.literal: first offenders stealing camels, horses, and cattle from the Qieliesi, are accomplices;
translations.idiomatic: first-time thieves of camels, horses, or cattle from the imperial herd count as accomplices;

sentences.zh: 略賣良人為奴婢一人；

translations.literal: abducting and selling one free person as slave or servant;
translations.idiomatic: abducting and selling one free person as a slave;

sentences.zh: 詐雕都省、行省印；

translations.literal: fraudulently carving the seals of the metropolitan and circuit secretariats;
translations.idiomatic: counterfeiting the seals of the metropolitan or circuit secretariats;

sentences.zh: 套畫省官押字，動支錢糧，幹礙選法；

translations.literal: tracing and painting provincial officials' signature marks, disbursing money and grain, interfering with selection law;
translations.idiomatic: forging provincial officials' signatures to disburse funds or interfere with appointment law;

sentences.zh: 或妄造妖言犯上：並杖一百七，流奴兒幹。

translations.literal: or rashly fabricating demonic words offending superiors: all receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff and exile to Nurgan.
translations.idiomatic: or fabricating seditious speech against the throne: all receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff and exile to Nurgan.

sentences.zh: 初犯盜駝馬牛，為首；

translations.literal: first offenders stealing camels, horses, and cattle, as ringleaders;
translations.idiomatic: First-time thieves of camels, horses, or cattle as ringleaders;

sentences.zh: 及盜財三百貫以上；

translations.literal: and theft of property of three hundred strings or more;
translations.idiomatic: and theft of property worth three hundred strings or more;

sentences.zh: 盜財十貫以下，經斷再犯；

translations.literal: theft of property of ten strings or less, already sentenced and reoffending;
translations.idiomatic: theft of ten strings or less after a prior conviction and reoffense;

sentences.zh: 發冢開棺傷屍，內應流者；

translations.literal: opening graves, opening coffins, and injuring corpses, inside accomplices who merit exile;
translations.idiomatic: grave robbery, opening coffins, and injuring corpses, including inside accomplices who merit exile;

sentences.zh: 挑剜裨湊寶鈔，以真作偽，再犯；

translations.literal: picking out and patching treasure notes, passing counterfeit as genuine, reoffense;
translations.idiomatic: carving and patching treasure notes to pass counterfeit as genuine, on reoffense;

sentences.zh: 知情買使偽鈔，三犯：並杖一百七，發肇州屯種。

translations.literal: knowingly buying and using counterfeit notes, three offenses: all receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff and are sent to Zhaozhou for agricultural exile.
translations.idiomatic: knowingly buying and using counterfeit notes on three offenses: all receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff and are sent to Zhaozhou for agricultural exile.

sentences.zh: 諸犯罪流遠逃歸，再獲，仍流。

translations.literal: In all cases where criminals exiled far flee and return, if captured again, they are still exiled.
translations.idiomatic: In all cases where exiles who fled their distant banishment are captured again, they are exiled once more.

sentences.zh: 若中路遭亂而逃，不再犯，及已老病並會赦者，釋之。

translations.literal: If they fled midway because of disorder, do not reoffend, and are already old or ill or meet amnesty, they are released.
translations.idiomatic: If they fled en route because of unrest, do not reoffend, and are aged, ill, or covered by amnesty, they are released.

sentences.zh: 諸流囚居役，非遇元正、寒食、重午等節，並勿給假。

translations.literal: In all cases of exiled prisoners on penal service, except when meeting New Year's Day, Cold Food, Double Fifth, and such festivals, leave is not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled prisoners on penal service receive no leave except on New Year's Day, Cold Food, Double Fifth, and similar festivals.

sentences.zh: 諸配役囚徒，遇閏月，通理之。

translations.literal: In all cases of prisoners on assigned service, intercalary months are counted fully.
translations.idiomatic: For prisoners on assigned penal service, intercalary months count in full toward the term.

sentences.zh: 諸應徒流，未行，會赦者釋之；

translations.literal: In all cases where penal servitude or exile should apply, if not yet carried out and amnesty occurs, they are released;
translations.idiomatic: Where penal servitude or exile has not yet begun and amnesty occurs, the offender is released;

sentences.zh: 已行未至，會赦者亦釋之。

translations.literal: if already underway but not yet arrived, and amnesty occurs, they are also released.
translations.idiomatic: if the sentence is underway but the destination not yet reached when amnesty occurs, release also applies.

sentences.zh: 諸囚徒配役，役所停罷者，會赦，免放。

translations.literal: In all cases where prisoners on assigned service have their place of service suspended, when amnesty occurs, they are pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Where penal service is suspended at the place of assignment, amnesty brings pardon and release.

sentences.zh: 諸有罪，奉旨流遠，雖會赦，非奏請不得放還。

translations.literal: In all cases where there is guilt and exile far is ordered by imperial command, even if amnesty occurs, they may not return without memorializing the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Those exiled far by imperial command may not return without a memorial to the throne, even under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諸徒罪，晝則帶鐐居役，夜則入囚牢房。

translations.literal: In all cases of penal servitude, by day they wear fetters while on service, by night they enter prison cells.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude convicts wear fetters by day while at labor and sleep in prison cells by night.

sentences.zh: 其流罪發各處屯種者，止令監臨關防屯種。

translations.literal: Those whose exile sends them to agricultural colonies at various places are only supervised and guarded in the colony planting.
translations.idiomatic: Those exiled to agricultural colonies are supervised only in planting and guarding the colony.

sentences.zh: 諸流遠囚徒，惟女直、高麗二族流湖廣，余並流奴兒幹及取海青之地。

translations.literal: In all cases of prisoners exiled far, only Jurchen and Goryeo peoples are exiled to Huguang; the rest are all exiled to Nurgan and places for taking sea eagles.
translations.idiomatic: Of those exiled far, only Jurchens and Koreans are sent to Huguang; all others go to Nurgan and the sea-eagle hunting grounds.

sentences.zh: 諸徒罪，無配役之所者，發鹽司居役。

translations.literal: In all cases of penal servitude where there is no place for assigned service, they are sent to salt offices for service.
translations.idiomatic: Where no local penal assignment exists, penal servitude convicts are sent to salt offices for labor.

sentences.zh: 諸主守失囚者，減囚罪三等，長押流囚官中路失囚者，視提牢官減主守罪四等，既斷還職。

translations.literal: In all cases where chief guards lose prisoners, their guilt is reduced three grades from the prisoner's crime; officials escorting exiled prisoners who lose them on the road see their guilt reduced four grades from the chief jail officer's guilt, and after judgment they return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Chief guards who lose prisoners are punished three grades below the prisoner's crime; escort officials who lose exiles en route are punished four grades below the chief jail officer's penalty and may return to office after judgment.

sentences.zh: 諸大小刑獄應監系之人，並送司獄司，分輕重監收。

translations.literal: In all cases of great and small criminal prisons, persons who should be imprisoned are all sent to the Prison Office and detained according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: All persons who should be imprisoned in criminal cases, great or small, are sent to the Prison Office and held according to severity.

sentences.zh: 諸掌刑獄，輒縱囚徒在禁飲博，及帶刀刃紙筆陰陽文字入禁者，罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where those in charge of prisons rashly permit prisoners to gamble and drink wine in detention, or bring blades, paper, brushes, or yin-yang texts into detention, they are punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jail officials who allow gambling or drinking in detention, or who permit blades, writing materials, or divination texts inside, are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸獄具，枷長五尺以上，六尺以下，闊一尺四寸以上，一尺六寸以下，死罪重二十五斤，徒流二十斤，杖罪一十五斤，皆以幹木為之，長闊輕重各刻誌其上。

translations.literal: In all cases of prison instruments, the cangue is five chi or more in length, six chi or less; one chi four cun or more in width, one chi six cun or less; for capital crimes twenty-five jin, for penal servitude and exile twenty jin, for rod crimes fifteen jin—all made of dry wood, with length, width, and weight each inscribed on them.
translations.idiomatic: Prison restraints: the cangue is five to six chi long and one chi four cun to one chi six cun wide; capital crimes bear twenty-five jin, penal servitude and exile twenty jin, rod offenses fifteen jin—all of dry wood with dimensions and weight marked on each.

sentences.zh: 杻長一尺六寸以上，二尺以下，橫三寸，厚一寸。

translations.literal: Shackles are one chi six cun or more in length, two chi or less; three cun across, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: Shackles are one chi six cun to two chi long, three cun wide and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 鎖長八尺以上，一丈二尺以下，鐐連環重三斤。

translations.literal: Locks are eight chi or more in length, one zhang two chi or less; linked fetters weigh three jin together.
translations.idiomatic: Locks are eight chi to one zhang two chi long; linked fetters together weigh three jin.

sentences.zh: 笞大頭徑二分七厘，小頭徑一分七厘，罪五十七以下用之。

translations.literal: The rod for flogging has a large end two fen seven li in diameter, small end one fen seven li—used for crimes of fifty-seven strokes or less.
translations.idiomatic: The flogging rod's large end is two fen seven li and the small end one fen seven li in diameter, for offenses of fifty-seven strokes or less.

sentences.zh: 杖大頭徑三分二厘，小頭徑二分二厘，罪六十七以上用之。

translations.literal: The staff has large end three fen two li, small end two fen two li—used for crimes of sixty-seven strokes or more.
translations.idiomatic: The beating staff's large end is three fen two li and the small end two fen two li, for offenses of sixty-seven strokes or more.

sentences.zh: 訊杖大頭徑四分五厘，小頭徑三分五厘，長三尺五寸，並刊削節目，無令筋膠諸物裝釘。

translations.literal: Interrogation staff large end four fen five li, small end three fen five li, length three chi five cun—all shaved with nodes, none may use sinew, glue, or other things to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: The interrogation staff is four fen five li at the large end, three fen five li at the small, three chi five cun long—all smoothed with nodes visible; sinew, glue, or other reinforcements are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 應決者，並用小頭，其決笞及杖者，臀受；

translations.literal: Where beating is applied, all use the small end; for flogging and staff beating, they receive it on the buttocks;
translations.idiomatic: All beatings strike with the small end; flogging and staff punishments are received on the buttocks;

sentences.zh: 拷訊者，臀若股分受，務令均停。

translations.literal: for torture interrogation, buttocks or thighs receive in turn, striving for evenness.
translations.idiomatic: under torture interrogation the buttocks or thighs alternate, distributed as evenly as possible.

sentences.zh: 諸郡縣佐貳及幕官，每月分番提牢，三日一親臨點視，其有枉禁及淹延者，即舉問。

translations.literal: In all cases, circuit deputy administrators and staff officials monthly take turns supervising the jail, every three days personally inspecting; where there is wrongful detention or delay, they are immediately reported.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit deputies and staff shall rotate monthly as jail supervisors, inspecting in person every three days; wrongful detention or delay is reported at once.

sentences.zh: 月終則具囚數牒次官，其在上都囚禁，從留守司提之。

translations.literal: At month's end they submit prisoner counts in a memo to the next official; for those imprisoned at the Upper Capital, the Commandery Office supervises.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end they report prisoner numbers to the next official in rank; at the Upper Capital the Commandery Office supervises imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 諸南北兵馬司，每月分番提牢，仍令提控案牘兼掌囚禁。

translations.literal: In all cases of north and south military horse offices, monthly turns supervising jail, still ordering record controllers to also manage imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: North and south military horse offices rotate monthly jail supervision and assign record controllers to manage imprisonment as well.

sentences.zh: 諸鹽運司監收鹽徒，每月佐貳官分番董視，與有司同。

translations.literal: In all cases of salt transport offices supervising salt convicts, monthly deputy officials take turns inspecting, same as regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: Salt transport offices supervising salt convicts require deputy officials to inspect in monthly rotation, as with regular offices.

sentences.zh: 諸內郡官仕雲南者，有罪依常律；

translations.literal: In all cases where inner circuit officials serve in Yunnan and commit crimes, regular law applies;
translations.idiomatic: Inner-circuit officials serving in Yunnan who commit crimes are judged under regular law;

sentences.zh: 土官有罪，罰而不廢。

translations.literal: native chiefs who commit crimes are punished but not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: native chiefs who commit crimes are punished but not removed from office.

sentences.zh: 諸左右兩江所部土官，輒興兵相仇殺者，坐以叛逆之罪。

translations.literal: In all cases where native chiefs under the Left and Right Two Rivers rashly raise troops to kill each other in feud, they are charged with rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Native chiefs of the Left and Right Two Rivers who rashly raise troops to feud and kill one another are charged with rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其有妄相告言者，以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: Where there are groundless mutual accusations, they are punished for that crime.
translations.idiomatic: Groundless mutual accusations are punished according to the offense alleged.

sentences.zh: 有司受財妄聽者，以枉法論。

translations.literal: Where officials accept bribes and heed groundless suits, it is judged as bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who take bribes and hear groundless suits are judged for bending the law.

sentences.zh: 諸土官有能愛撫軍民，境內寧謐者，三年一次，保勘升官。

translations.literal: In all cases where native chiefs can cherish and comfort troops and civilians and the territory is tranquil, once every three years they are recommended for investigation and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Native chiefs who cherish troops and civilians and keep the territory tranquil may be recommended for promotion once every three years.

sentences.zh: 其有勛勞，及應升賞承襲，文字至帥府，輒非理疏駁，故為難阻者，罷之。

translations.literal: Where they have merit and should be promoted, rewarded, or inherit, and documents reach the marshal's headquarters but are groundlessly rejected or deliberately obstructed, [the officials] are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Where merit warrants promotion, reward, or inheritance and documents reach the marshal's headquarters are groundlessly rejected or deliberately obstructed, the obstructing officials are dismissed.

sentences.zh: ○祭令

translations.literal: ○ Sacrificial Regulations
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial Regulations

sentences.zh: 諸國家有事於效廟，凡獻官及百執事之人，受誓戒之後，散齊宿於正寢，致齊於祀所。

translations.literal: In all cases where the state has affairs at the ancestral temple, all offering officials and the hundred functionaries, after receiving the oath and abstinence, during dispersed abstinence lodge in the main quarters, during concentrated abstinence at the sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: When the state has rites at the ancestral temple, all offering officials and functionaries, after taking the oath of abstinence, lodge in the main quarters during dispersed abstinence and at the sacrifice site during concentrated abstinence.

sentences.zh: 散齊日治事如故，不吊喪問疾，不作樂，不判署刑殺文字，不決罰罪人，不與穢惡事。

translations.literal: On dispersed-abstinence days they conduct affairs as usual, do not condole at funerals or inquire after illness, do not make music, do not sign documents on punishment and execution, do not sentence criminals, and do not engage in defiling or vile matters.
translations.idiomatic: During dispersed abstinence they conduct business as usual but do not mourn, inquire after the sick, make music, sign execution documents, sentence criminals, or engage in defiling matters.

sentences.zh: 致齊日惟祀事得行，余悉禁之。

translations.literal: On concentrated-abstinence days only sacrificial affairs may proceed; all else is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: During concentrated abstinence only sacrificial affairs may proceed; all else is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸嶽鎮名山，國家之所秩祀，小民輒僭禮犯義，以祈禱褻瀆者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of famous mountains and sacred peaks that the state ranks for sacrifice, if commoners rashly usurp ritual and violate propriety to pray and blaspheme, it is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Where the state ranks famous mountains and peaks for sacrifice, commoners who usurp ritual, violate propriety, or pray in blasphemy are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸五嶽、四瀆、五鎮，國家秩祀有常，諸王公主駙馬輒遣人降香致祭者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of the Five Peaks, Four Rivers, and Five Marchmounts where state sacrifice is fixed, if princes, princesses, or imperial sons-in-law rashly send persons to descend incense and offer sacrifice, it is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: At the Five Peaks, Four Rivers, and Five Marchmounts where state sacrifice is fixed, princes, princesses, or imperial sons-in-law who send persons to offer incense are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸郡縣宣聖廟，凡官員使臣軍馬，輒敢館谷於內，有司輒敢聽訟宴飲於內，工官輒敢營造於內，並行禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of Confucius temples in circuits and districts, if officials, envoys, or troops and horses rashly dare lodge within, if officials rashly dare hear lawsuits or feast and drink within, if craftsmen rashly dare build within—all are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: At circuit and district Confucius temples, officials, envoys, or troops who lodge within, officials who hear lawsuits or feast within, or craftsmen who build within—all are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸書院同。

translations.literal: In all cases of academies, the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same applies to academies.

sentences.zh: 諸每月朔望，郡縣長吏率其參佐僚屬，詣孔子廟拜謁禮畢，從學官升堂講說。

translations.literal: In all cases on the first and fifteenth of each month, district and circuit chief administrators lead their assistants and subordinates to the Confucius temple to pay respects; when the rites are complete, they follow the education officials up to the hall for lecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month, district and circuit chiefs lead their staff to the Confucius temple; when the rites are done, they follow education officials to the hall for lecture.

sentences.zh: 其鄉村市鎮，亦擇有學問德行可為師長者，於農隙之時，以教導民。

translations.literal: In villages and market towns as well, they also select persons of learning and moral conduct who can serve as teachers; in the slack season of farming they instruct the people.
translations.idiomatic: Villages and market towns likewise select learned persons of moral conduct as teachers to instruct the people in the farming slack season.

sentences.zh: 其有視為迂緩而不務者，糾之。

translations.literal: Where any treat this as pedantic and slow and do not practice it, they are reported and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who treat this as pedantic and neglect it are reported and prosecuted.

sentences.zh: ○學規

translations.literal: ○ School Regulations
translations.idiomatic: School Regulations

sentences.zh: 諸蒙古、漢人國子監學官任內，驗其教養出格生員多寡，以為升遷。

translations.literal: In all cases of Mongol and Han Directorate of Education school officials during their tenure, the number of outstanding students they nurture is verified for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol and Han Directorate school officials are promoted according to how many outstanding students they produce in office.

sentences.zh: 博士教授有闕，從監察御史舉之，其不稱職者黜之，坐及元舉之官。

translations.literal: Where doctorate instructors lack someone, the surveillance censor recommends; those unfit are dismissed, and the originally recommending official shares guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Vacant doctorate and instructor posts are filled on recommendation by the surveillance censor; the unfit are dismissed and the recommender shares guilt.

sentences.zh: 諸國子生悖慢師長、及行禮失儀、言行不謹、講誦不熟、功課不辦、無故廢學、有故不告輒出、告假違限、執事失誤、忿戾鬥爭，並委正、錄糾舉。

translations.literal: In all cases of Directorate students who are disrespectful to teachers, breach ritual deportment, are careless in speech and conduct, are unskilled in recitation, fail coursework, abandon study without cause, leave without reporting when there is cause, exceed leave limits, err in duties, or are angry and quarrelsome—all are entrusted to the Rectors and Recorders for reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students who disrespect teachers, breach ritual, speak or act carelessly, fail recitation or coursework, abandon study without cause, leave without leave, exceed leave limits, err in duties, or quarrel—all are reported by the Rectors and Recorders.

sentences.zh: 除悖慢師長別議，余者初犯戒諭，再犯、三犯約量責罰。

translations.literal: Except disrespect to teachers which is separately adjudged, for the rest first offense earns admonition, second and third offenses entail measured punishment as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Disrespect to teachers is adjudged separately; other offenses earn admonition on the first offense and measured punishment on the second and third.

sentences.zh: 其廚人、仆夫、門子，常切在學，供給使令，違者就便決責。

translations.literal: Cooks, servants, and gatekeepers must constantly be at school to supply and serve orders; violators may be immediately beaten on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Cooks, servants, and gatekeepers must remain at school to serve; violators may be beaten on the spot.

sentences.zh: 諸國學居首善之地，六館諸生，以次升齋，毋或躐等。

translations.literal: In all cases the Directorate occupies the foremost place of excellence; students of the six halls advance to halls in order, none may leap ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate holds the foremost place of learning; students of the six halls advance in order and may not skip ranks.

sentences.zh: 其有未應升而求升，及曾犯學規者，輕者降之，重者黜之。

translations.literal: Where any not yet qualified seek advancement, or have violated school regulations, the light are demoted, the heavy expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Those unqualified who seek advancement, or who have violated school regulations, are demoted if the offense is light and expelled if heavy.

sentences.zh: 其教之不以道者，監察御史糾之。

translations.literal: Those who teach not by the Way are reported by the surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors who teach not by the Way are reported by the surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 諸國子監私試積分生員，其有不事課業，及一切違戾規矩，初犯罰一分，再犯罰二分，三犯除名。

translations.literal: In all cases of Directorate private-exam point students, those who neglect coursework or violate any regulations, first offense deduct one point, second two points, third expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate private-exam students who neglect coursework or violate regulations lose one point on the first offense, two on the second, and are expelled on the third.

sentences.zh: 已補高等生員，其有違戾規矩，初犯殿試一年，再犯除名，並從學正、錄糾舉。

translations.literal: For advanced-tier students who violate regulations, first offense deferred one year in palace exam, second expulsion—all reported by academic rectifiers and recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced-tier students who violate regulations are deferred one year in the palace exam on the first offense and expelled on the second, as reported by academic rectifiers and recorders.

sentences.zh: 正、錄知見不糾舉者，從本監議罰。

translations.literal: Where Rectors and Recorders knew and did not report, the Directorate deliberates punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Rectors and Recorders who knew and failed to report are punished by Directorate deliberation.

sentences.zh: 在學生員，歲終實歷坐齋不滿半周歲者，並除名。

translations.literal: Students in residence at year end whose actual sitting in hall is less than half a year—all expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Students who at year end have sat in hall less than half a year are all expelled.

sentences.zh: 除月假外，其餘告假，不用準算，學正、錄歲終通行考較。

translations.literal: Apart from monthly leave, other leave does not count toward calculation; academic rectifiers and recorders compare fully at year end.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from monthly leave, other leave does not count; academic rectifiers and recorders conduct a full comparison at year end.

sentences.zh: 漢人生員，三年不能通一經，及不肯篤勤者，勒令出學。

translations.literal: Han students who in three years cannot master one classic, or are unwilling to study diligently, are ordered to leave school.
translations.idiomatic: Han students who in three years cannot master one classic, or refuse diligent study, are ordered to leave school.

sentences.zh: 諸奎章閣授經郎生員，每月朔望上弦下弦，給假四日；

translations.literal: In all cases of Kui Zhang Pavilion scripture instructors' students, on new moon, full moon, first quarter, last quarter—four days leave each month;
translations.idiomatic: Kui Zhang Pavilion scripture students receive four days' leave each month on new moon, full moon, and the two quarter moons;

sentences.zh: 當入宿衛者，給假三日；

translations.literal: those due to enter palace guard service—three days leave;
translations.idiomatic: those due for palace guard duty receive three days' leave;

sentences.zh: 余有故須請假者，於授經郎稟說，附歷給假。

translations.literal: for other causes needing leave, they report to the scripture instructor, recorded in the register and leave granted.
translations.idiomatic: for other justified leave they report to the scripture instructor and receive recorded leave.

sentences.zh: 無故不入學，第一次罰當日會食，第二次於師席前罰拜及當日會食，第三次於學士院及師席前罰拜及當日會食，三次不改，奏聞懲戒黜退。

translations.literal: Without cause not entering study: first time forfeit that day's communal meal; second time bowing punishment before teacher's seat and forfeit communal meal; third time before the Academy of Scholars and teacher's seat bowing punishment and forfeit communal meal; three times unchanged, memorialized for disciplinary expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Unexcused absence: first offense forfeits the day's communal meal; second adds bowing punishment before the teacher's seat and forfeiture of the meal; third adds bowing before the Academy of Scholars and the teacher's seat; after three unchanged offenses, memorialized for expulsion.

sentences.zh: 諸隨路學校，計其錢糧多寡，養育生徒，提調正官時一詣學督視，必使課講有程，訓迪有法，賞勤罰惰，作成人材，其學政不舉者究之。

translations.literal: In all cases of circuit schools, accounting money and grain to support students, the supervising chief official periodically visits to oversee, must ensure scheduled lectures, proper instruction, reward diligence and punish sloth, nurture talent—those whose academic governance fails are investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit schools shall account for funds to support students; the supervising chief shall visit periodically to ensure scheduled lectures, sound instruction, rewards for diligence and punishment for sloth, and the nurturing of talent—failure in academic governance is investigated.

sentences.zh: 諸教官在任，侵資錢糧，荒廢廟宇，教養無實，行止不臧，有忝師席，從廉訪司糾之；

translations.literal: In all cases where instructors in office embezzle funds and grain, neglect temple buildings, nurture without substance, conduct is unworthy and disgraces the teacher's seat—reported by surveillance commission;
translations.idiomatic: Instructors who embezzle school funds, neglect temple buildings, teach without substance, or conduct themselves unworthily of the teacher's seat are reported by the surveillance commission;

sentences.zh: 任滿，有司輒朦朧給由者究之。

translations.literal: at term's end if offices rashly give credentials vaguely, investigated.
translations.idiomatic: offices that vaguely issue credentials at term's end are also investigated.

sentences.zh: 諸贍學田土，學官職吏或賣熟為荒，減額收租，或受財縱令豪右占佃，陷沒兼並，及巧名冒支者，提調官究之。

translations.literal: In all cases of school-support lands, if school officials or clerks sell ripe as waste, reduce quota rent, or take bribes to let powerful families occupy and merge, or falsely claim disbursements—investigated by supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: School-support lands misused by officials or clerks who declare fertile land waste, reduce rent quotas, take bribes to let powerful families occupy or merge land, or falsely claim disbursements are investigated by the supervising official.

sentences.zh: 諸貧寒老病之士，必為眾所尊敬者，保申本路體覆無異，下本學養贍，仍移廉訪司察之；

translations.literal: In all cases of poor, aged, ill scholars whom the multitude must respect, recommended to the circuit with verification, sent down to local school for support, still referred to surveillance commission for inspection;
translations.idiomatic: Poor, aged, or ill scholars respected by the community may be recommended to the circuit for verification and supported by the local school, with inspection by the surveillance commission;

sentences.zh: 但有冒濫，從提調官改正。

translations.literal: but if fraudulent, corrected by supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: fraudulent cases are corrected by the supervising official.

sentences.zh: 諸各處學校，為講習作養之地，有司輒侵借其錢糧者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of schools everywhere as places for study and nurturing, if offices rashly borrow their funds and grain, forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Schools are places of study and nurturing; offices that borrow their funds or grain are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 教官不稱職者，廉訪司糾之。

translations.literal: Instructors unfit for office are reported by surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: Unfit instructors are reported by the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 諸在任及已代教官，輒攜家入學，褻瀆居止者，從廉訪司糾之。

translations.literal: In all cases of instructors in office or former instructors who rashly bring families into school and defile residence, reported by surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors in office or former instructors who bring their families into school and defile the premises are reported by the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 諸各路醫學大小生員，不令坐齋肄業，有名無實，及在學而訓誨無法，課講鹵莽，茍應故事者，教授、正、錄、提調官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In all cases of circuit medical school large and small students not made to sit hall and study, name without substance, or in school but instruction lawless, lectures careless, perfunctorily following form—professor, rectifier, recorder, supervising official fined salary by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit medical students not made to study in hall, holding rank without substance, or taught carelessly and perfunctorily incur graduated salary fines for professor, rectifier, recorder, and supervising official.

sentences.zh: 諸醫人於十三科內，不能精通一科者，不得行醫。

translations.literal: In all cases where medical practitioners within the thirteen branches cannot master one branch, they may not practice medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Medical practitioners who cannot master one of the thirteen branches may not practice medicine.

sentences.zh: 太醫院不精加考試，輒以私妄舉充隨朝太醫及內外郡縣醫官，內外郡縣醫學不依法考試，輒縱人行醫者，並從監察御史廉訪司察之。

translations.literal: If the Imperial Medical Institute does not carefully examine but rashly and privately recommends court physicians and inner/outer circuit and district medical officers, or circuit and district medical schools do not examine by law but rashly permit practice—all investigated by surveillance censor and surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: If the Imperial Medical Institute recommends court or circuit physicians without careful examination, or medical schools permit practice without lawful examination, the surveillance censor and commission shall investigate.

sentences.zh: ○軍律

translations.literal: ○ Military Law
translations.idiomatic: Military Law

sentences.zh: 諸軍官離職、屯軍離營、行軍離其部伍者，皆有罪。

translations.literal: In all cases military officers leave post, garrison soldiers leave camp, soldiers on march leave their unit—all guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers who leave post, garrison soldiers who leave camp, and marching soldiers who leave their unit are all guilty.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官不得擅離部署。

translations.literal: In all cases military officers may not rashly leave deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers may not leave their deployment without authorization.

sentences.zh: 赴闕言事，有必合言者，實封附遞以聞。

translations.literal: To go to court to speak on affairs, where there is matter that must be spoken, seal truly and send by courier to report.
translations.idiomatic: To petition the throne on necessary matters, seal the memorial and send it by courier.

sentences.zh: 諸隨處軍馬，有久遠營屯，或時暫經過，並從官給糧食，輒妨擾農民、阻滯客旅者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases wherever troops and horses have long-standing camps or temporary passage, all receive government grain; those who rashly harass farmers or obstruct travelers are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Troops in long camps or on passage receive government grain; harassing farmers or obstructing travelers is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸臨陣先退者，處死。

translations.literal: In all cases of retreating first in battle array, death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Retreating first in battle is punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 諸統軍捕逐寇盜，分守要害，約相為聲援，稽留失期，致殺死將士，仍不即追襲者，處死，雖會赦，罷職不敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where commanders pursue and capture bandits, divide to guard key points, agree mutual support, linger past deadline causing death of officers and soldiers, still do not immediately pursue—death penalty; even if amnesty, dismissed without reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders who fail to support one another, miss deadlines causing deaths, and do not immediately pursue bandits are executed; even under amnesty they are dismissed without reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸軍民官，鎮守邊陲，帥兵擊賊，紀律無統，變易號令，背約失期，形分勢路，致令破軍殺將，或未戰逃歸，或棄城退走，復能建招徠之功者，減其罪，無功者，各以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases of civil and military officials guarding borders, leading troops against bandits, discipline without unity, changing orders, breaking agreements missing deadlines, scattered forces split routes causing routed armies and slain generals, or fleeing without battle, or abandoning cities and retreating—if afterward they can achieve recovery and recruitment merit, sentence reduced; without merit, each punished for their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials who lead troops without discipline, change orders, miss deadlines, scatter forces, rout armies, flee without fighting, or abandon cities—but later achieve recovery—have sentences reduced; without such merit, each is punished for his crime.

sentences.zh: 諸防戍軍人於屯所逃者，杖一百七，再犯者處死。

translations.literal: In all cases of garrison soldiers fleeing from stockade, one hundred seven strokes; repeat offenders death.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison soldiers who flee the stockade receive one hundred seven strokes of the staff; repeat offenders are executed.

sentences.zh: 若科定出征，逃匿者，斬以徇。

translations.literal: If mobilized for campaign and they flee and hide, beheaded to warn others.
translations.idiomatic: Those mobilized for campaign who flee and hide are beheaded as an example.

sentences.zh: 諸軍戶貧乏已經存恤而復逃者，杖八十七，發遣當軍。

translations.literal: In all cases of military households impoverished already relieved yet flee again, eighty-seven strokes, sent to serve as soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished military households already relieved who flee again receive eighty-seven strokes and are sent back to service.

sentences.zh: 隱藏者減二等，兩鄰知而不首者，又減隱藏罪二等。

translations.literal: Concealers reduced two grades; neighbors on both sides who knew and did not report, again reduced two grades from concealer's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Concealers are punished two grades lighter; neighbors on both sides who knew and failed to report are punished two grades below the concealer.

sentences.zh: 諸軍戶告乏求替者，從有司覆實之，其詐妄者，廉訪司憲之。

translations.literal: In all cases of military households reporting destitution seeking replacement, follow offices to verify; if fraudulent, surveillance commission punishes.
translations.idiomatic: Military households reporting destitution to seek replacement are verified by the proper offices; fraud is punished by the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 諸各衛扈從漢軍，每戶選練習壯丁一人常充，仍於貼戶內選兩人輪番供役，其有故必合替換者，自萬戶至於百戶，相視所換之可用，然後用之。

translations.literal: In all cases of each guard's attendant Han troops, each household selects one practiced strong youth for constant duty; still from attached households select two for rotating service; where replacement is necessary, from ten-thousand-household to hundred-household they examine whether replacement is usable, then employ.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard's attendant Han troops select one practiced strong youth per household for constant duty and two from attached households for rotation; replacements from hundred- to ten-thousand-household rank must be examined for fitness before use.

sentences.zh: 百戶、千戶、萬戶私換者，驗名數多寡，論罪解降。

translations.literal: Hundred-, thousand-, ten-thousand-households who privately replace—verify names and numbers, judge guilt and demote or dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: Hundred-, thousand-, and ten-thousand-household officers who make private replacements are judged by numbers involved and demoted or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸管軍官吏，受錢代替軍空名者，驗入己錢數，以枉法科罪除名。

translations.literal: In all cases of military-administering officials who take money to substitute empty soldier names—verify money taken for self, sentenced for bending law and removed from roster.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials who take money to fill empty soldier rolls are sentenced for bending the law according to the amount taken and removed from the roster.

sentences.zh: 令兄弟子侄驅丁代替者，驗名數多寡，論罪解降。

translations.literal: Ordering brothers, sons, nephews, or servants to substitute—verify names and numbers, judge guilt and demote or dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: Those who substitute brothers, sons, nephews, or servants are judged by numbers involved and demoted or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸軍馬征伐，虜掠良民，凶徒射利，略賣人口，或自賊殺，或以病亡棄屍道路、暴骸溝壑者，嚴行禁止。

translations.literal: In all cases when army and horses campaign, plundering good people, wicked persons profiting, abducting and selling population, or killing themselves, or abandoning corpses on roads from illness, exposing bones in ditches—strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, plundering civilians, profiteering, abducting and selling people, murder, or abandoning corpses on roads and exposing bones in ditches are strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: ○戶婚

translations.literal: ○ Households and Marriage
translations.idiomatic: Households and Marriage

sentences.zh: 諸匠戶子女，使男習工事，女習黹繡，其輒敢拘刷者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of artisan-household sons and daughters, males are to learn craft work and females embroidery and stitching; whoever rashly seizes and drafts them—this is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and daughters of artisan households must have boys trained in craft work and girls in embroidery; anyone who rashly seizes and drafts them is forbidden to do so.

sentences.zh: 諸系官當差人戶，非奉朝省文字，輒投充諸王及各投下給使者，論罪。

translations.literal: In all cases of households registered as official corvée households, without documents from the court and ministries rashly entering service of princes and each appanage as supply agents—sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: Official corvée households who serve princes or appanage agents without authorization from the court and ministries are punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 諸僧道還俗，兄弟析居，奴放為良，未入於籍者，應諸王諸子公主駙馬毋拘藏之。

translations.literal: In all cases of monks and Taoists returning to lay life, brothers dividing households, slaves released as commoners, not yet entered in registers—princes, imperial sons, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law must not detain and conceal them.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Taoists who return to lay life, brothers who divide households, slaves manumitted to commoner status, and persons not yet entered in the registers must not be detained or concealed by princes, imperial sons, princesses, or sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 民有敢隱藏者，罪之。

translations.literal: Civilians who dare conceal them—punished.
translations.idiomatic: Any commoner who conceals them is punished.

sentences.zh: 諸庶民有妄以漏籍戶及土田於諸王公主駙馬呈獻者，論罪；

translations.literal: In all cases where commoners rashly present unregistered households and land to princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law—sentenced;
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who rashly present unregistered households or land to princes, princesses, or imperial sons-in-law are punished according to law;

sentences.zh: 諸投下輒濫收者，亦罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where appanage holders rashly accept them indiscriminately—also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Appanage holders who indiscriminately accept them are likewise punished.

sentences.zh: 諸官吏占人戶供給私用者，治罪。

translations.literal: In all cases where officials seize households to supply private needs—punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who seize households for their private supply are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸有司治賦斂急，致貧民鬻男女為輸者，追還所鬻男女，而正有司罪，價勿償。

translations.literal: In all cases where offices administer tax levies urgently, causing poor people to sell sons and daughters for payment—return the sold sons and daughters, correct the offices' crime; the price is not compensated.
translations.idiomatic: Where officials levy taxes so harshly that the poor sell sons or daughters to pay, the children sold are returned, the officials are punished, and the purchase price is not repaid.

sentences.zh: 諸生女溺死者，沒其家財之半以勞軍。

translations.literal: In all cases of drowning infant daughters, confiscate half the household property to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Those who drown infant daughters forfeit half their household property to support the army.

sentences.zh: 首者為奴，即以為良。

translations.literal: The principal offender is enslaved; the informant is immediately made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The principal offender is enslaved; the informant is immediately granted commoner status.

sentences.zh: 有司失舉者，罪之。

translations.literal: Offices that fail to report—punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who fail to report the offense are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸民戶流移，所在有司起遣復業，輒以闌遺人收之者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of civilian households migrating, wherever offices send them to resume livelihood, whoever rashly uses vagrants to seize and accept them—prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: When migrating households are sent home by local offices to resume livelihood, seizing them as stray or lost persons is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸鰥寡孤獨，老弱殘疾，窮而無告者，於養濟院收養。

translations.literal: In all cases of widowers, widows, orphans, and solitaries, the aged, weak, and disabled, destitute with no recourse—received and cared for at relief hospices.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and others without support, together with the aged, infirm, and disabled who are destitute and helpless, are to be received and maintained at relief hospices.

sentences.zh: 應收養而不收養，不應收養而收養者，罪其守宰，按治官常糾察之。

translations.literal: Those who should be taken in but are not, or should not be taken in but are—magistrates are punished; investigating officials regularly scrutinize.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who fail to take in those who should be sheltered, or who shelter those who should not be, are punished; investigating officials are to scrutinize this regularly.

sentences.zh: 諸被災流民，有司招諭復業。

translations.literal: In all cases of disaster refugees, offices summon and persuade them to resume livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster refugees are to be summoned and persuaded by the proper offices to resume their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 其年深不能復業及失所在者，蠲其賦。

translations.literal: Those long unable to resume livelihood and those whose whereabouts are lost—their taxes are remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who after long absence cannot resume livelihood, and those whose whereabouts are unknown, are exempted from tax.

sentences.zh: 輒抑民包納者，從臺憲官糾之。

translations.literal: Those who rashly coerce people to cover payments—the censorate investigates.
translations.idiomatic: Those who coerce commoners to cover others' tax payments are investigated by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 諸年谷不熟，人民轉徙，所至既經賑濟，復聚黨持仗，剽劫財物，毆傷平民者，除孤老殘疾不能自贍，任便居住，有司依前存養，其餘有子弟者，驗其家口，計程遠近，支與行糧，次第押還元籍，沿路復為民害者，從所在有司斷遣。

translations.literal: In all cases when annual grain is not ripe and people migrate, wherever they arrive having already been relieved yet again assemble gangs bearing weapons, plunder goods, and beat and injure civilians—except orphans, the aged, and disabled unable to support themselves, permitted to dwell at will and offices maintain them as before; the rest who have sons and younger kin, verify household size, calculate journey distance, disburse travel grain, and in order escort back to original register; those who again harm civilians along the road—follow local offices to judge and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: When harvests fail and people migrate, those who after relief still band together armed to plunder and injure civilians—except orphans, the aged, and disabled who cannot support themselves, who may remain and be maintained as before—all others with dependents receive travel grain according to household size and distance and are escorted back to their original registration in order; those who harm civilians along the route are judged and disposed of by local authorities.

sentences.zh: 諸蒙古、回回、契丹、女直、漢人軍前所俘人口，留家者為奴婢，居外附籍者即為良民，已居外復認為奴婢者，沒入其家財。

translations.literal: In all cases of Mongols, Muslims, Khitan, Jurchen, and Han populations captured before the army: those kept at home are slave servants; those living outside and attaching to registers are immediately commoners; those already living outside who again claim them as slave servants—forfeit household property.
translations.idiomatic: Among Mongols, Muslims, Khitan, Jurchen, and Han taken captive in campaign, those kept at home remain bond servants; those living outside and registered become commoners; anyone who, after they live outside, again claims them as bond servants forfeits his household property.

sentences.zh: 諸收捕叛亂軍人，掠取生口，並從按治官及軍民官一同審閱，實為賊黨妻屬者，給公據付之，無公據者，以掠良民之罪罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases of capturing rebel soldiers and seizing captives, jointly with investigating officials and military-civilian officials review together; if truly wives and kin of bandits, issue public certificate and deliver; without public certificate—sentence for seizing good people.
translations.idiomatic: Captives taken when suppressing rebels must be jointly reviewed by investigating officials and military-civilian officers; wives and dependents of bandits are released with a public certificate; without a certificate, the taker is sentenced for seizing commoners.

sentences.zh: 諸群盜降附，以所劫掠男女充收捕官饋獻者，勿受，仍還為民。

translations.literal: In all cases where bandits who surrender present men and women plundered as gifts to arresting officials—do not accept; still return them as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When surrendered bandits offer plundered men and women as gifts to arresting officials, the gift is not accepted and the persons are returned to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 無親屬可收系者，使男女相配，聽為民。

translations.literal: Those with no kin to receive them—pair men and women and permit them to be commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Those with no kin to take them in are paired in marriage and permitted to live as commoners.

sentences.zh: 其留賊所者，悉縱之。

translations.literal: Those remaining with the bandits—all release them.
translations.idiomatic: Those still held by the bandits are all released.

sentences.zh: 諸收到被掠婦人，忘其鄉里，並無親屬可歸者，有司與之嫁聘，所得聘財，與資妝束。

translations.literal: In all cases of receiving plundered women who forget their native place and have no kin to return to—offices provide marriage betrothal; betrothal wealth obtained is given as dowry outfit.
translations.idiomatic: Plundered women who cannot recall their home or kin are given marriage arrangements by the proper offices; betrothal payments received are applied to their dowry.

sentences.zh: 諸軍民官輒隱藏降附人民，不令復業者，罪之。

translations.literal: In all cases where military-civilian officials rashly conceal surrendered people and do not let them resume livelihood—punished.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civilian officials who conceal surrendered people and prevent them from resuming livelihood are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸籍沒人口，元主私典賣者，追收入官，征價還主。

translations.literal: In all cases of confiscated population originally privately pawned or sold by the owner—recover into government, collect price and return to owner.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscated persons who were privately pawned or sold by their original owner are recovered for the state; the price is collected and returned to the owner.

sentences.zh: 諸投下官員，招占已籍系官民匠戶計者，沒其家財，所占戶歸本籍。

translations.literal: In all cases of appanage officials who entice and seize already-registered official, civilian, and artisan households—forfeit household property; seized households return to original register.
translations.idiomatic: Appanage officials who entice away registered official, civilian, or artisan households forfeit their property; the seized households return to their original registration.

sentences.zh: 諸投下所籍戶，令出五戶絲，余悉勿與。

translations.literal: In all cases of households registered to appanages, order them to pay only the five-households silk levy; the rest is not given.
translations.idiomatic: Households registered to an appanage pay only the five-households silk levy; no other exactions are permitted.

sentences.zh: 其有橫斂於民，從臺憲究之。

translations.literal: Those who indiscriminately levy on the people—the censorate investigates.
translations.idiomatic: Those who levy exactions arbitrarily on the people are investigated by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 諸願棄俗出家為僧道，若本戶丁多，差役不闕，及有兄弟足以侍養父母者，於本籍有司陳請，保勘申路，給據簪剃，違者斷罪歸俗。

translations.literal: In all cases of wishing to leave the world and become monk or Taoist, if the household has many adult males, corvée is not lacking, and there are brothers enough to serve parents—petition the register office of origin, guarantee and verify, report to the circuit, issue certificate and tonsure; violators are sentenced and returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to become monks or Taoists, where the household has sufficient adult males for corvée and brothers to support the parents, must petition the local register office, obtain guaranty and verification, and receive tonsure certificate from the circuit; violators are sentenced and returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 諸河西僧人有妻子者，當差發、稅糧、鋪馬、次舍與庶民同。

translations.literal: In all cases of Hexi monks who have wives, corvée dispatch, tax grain, relay horses, and lodging are the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi monks who have wives bear corvée, tax grain, relay horses, and lodging duties the same as commoners.

sentences.zh: 其無妻子者，蠲除之。

translations.literal: Those without wives—exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Those without wives are exempted.

sentences.zh: 諸父母在，分財異居，父母困乏，不共子職，及同宗有服之親，鰥寡孤獨，老弱殘疾，不能自存，寄食養濟院，不行收養者，重議其罪。

translations.literal: In all cases where parents are alive yet property is divided and households separated, parents are destitute and children do not share filial duty, and among same-clan kin within mourning, widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, aged, weak, and disabled unable to support themselves who lodge at relief hospices yet are not taken in—their crime is heavily reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Where parents live but sons divide property and live apart while parents are destitute, or where widowed, orphaned, aged, or disabled kin within mourning who cannot support themselves lodge at relief hospices yet are not sheltered, the offense is heavily reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 親族亦貧不能給者，許養濟院收錄。

translations.literal: Kin also poor and unable to provide—permit relief hospices to receive and record.
translations.idiomatic: Where kin are too poor to provide, relief hospices may receive and register them.

sentences.zh: 諸典賣田宅，從有司給據立契，買主賣主隨時赴有司推收稅糧。

translations.literal: In all cases of pawning or selling fields and houses, follow the proper offices to issue certificate and establish contract; buyer and seller at once attend offices to transfer and collect tax grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pawning or selling fields and houses requires a certificate and contract from the proper offices; buyer and seller must promptly attend the offices to transfer registration and pay tax grain.

sentences.zh: 若買主權豪，官吏阿徇，不即過割，止令賣主納稅，或為分派別戶包納，或為立詭名，但受分文之贓，笞五十七，仍於買主名下，驗元價追征，以半沒官，半付告者。

translations.literal: If the buyer is powerful, officials curry favor, and do not promptly transfer registration but only make the seller pay tax, or assign to another household to cover payment, or establish false names yet only receive bribe portions—fifty-seven strokes; still under the buyer's name verify original price and pursue collection, half confiscated to government, half to accuser.
translations.idiomatic: If a powerful buyer or colluding official fails to transfer registration, makes the seller pay tax alone, assigns payment to another household, or uses a false name while taking bribes—fifty-seven strokes; the original price is still pursued from the buyer, half confiscated to the state and half to the accuser.

sentences.zh: 首領官及所掌吏，斷罪罷役。

translations.literal: Leading officials and clerks in charge—sentenced and dismissed from service.
translations.idiomatic: The leading official and responsible clerks are sentenced and dismissed from service.

sentences.zh: 諸典賣田宅，須從尊長書押，給據立帳，歷問有服房親及鄰人典主，不願交易者，限十日批退，違限不批退者，笞一十七。

translations.literal: In all cases of pawning or selling fields and houses, must follow senior kin to sign and seal, issue certificate and establish account, inquire of kin within mourning, neighbors, and pawn masters; those unwilling to trade—limit ten days to mark refusal; exceeding the limit without marking refusal—seventeen strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Pawning or selling fields and houses requires senior kin to sign and seal, a certificate and account, and inquiry of mourning kin, neighbors, and pawn masters; unwilling parties have ten days to mark refusal; failure within the limit—seventeen strokes.

sentences.zh: 願者限十五日議價，立契成交，違限不酬價者，笞二十七。

translations.literal: Those willing—limit fifteen days to negotiate price and establish contract to complete; exceeding limit without paying price—twenty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Willing parties have fifteen days to set price and complete the contract; failure to pay within the limit—twenty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 任便交易，親鄰典主故相邀阻，需求書字錢物者，笞二十七。

translations.literal: Permit free trade; kin, neighbors, and pawn masters who deliberately obstruct and demand writing fees or goods—twenty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Trade is otherwise free; kin, neighbors, or pawn masters who deliberately obstruct and demand fees or goods—twenty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 業主虛張高價，不相由問成交者，笞三十七，仍聽親鄰典主百日收贖，限外不得爭訴。

translations.literal: Owners who falsely inflate high price and complete without inquiry—thirty-seven strokes; still permit kin, neighbors, and pawn masters to redeem within one hundred days; beyond the limit no litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Owners who inflate price and complete sale without inquiry—thirty-seven strokes; kin, neighbors, and pawn masters may still redeem within one hundred days; after that, no suit lies.

sentences.zh: 業主欺昧，故不交業者，笞四十七。

translations.literal: Owners who deceive and deliberately do not deliver the property—forty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Owners who deceive and refuse to deliver the property—forty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 親鄰典主在他所者，百里之外，不在由問之限。

translations.literal: Kin, neighbors, and pawn masters in other places beyond one hundred li are not within the inquiry limit.
translations.idiomatic: Kin, neighbors, and pawn masters more than one hundred li away are not subject to the inquiry requirement.

sentences.zh: 若違例事覺，有司不以理聽斷者，監察御史廉訪司糾之。

translations.literal: If violations come to light and offices do not hear and judge according to principle, surveillance censors and surveillance commission investigate.
translations.idiomatic: If violations are discovered and the proper offices fail to judge fairly, the censorate and surveillance commission investigate.

sentences.zh: 諸軍官軍人不歸營屯，到任官員不歸官舍，往來使臣不歸館驛，輒於民家居止，為民害者，行省行臺起遣究治。

translations.literal: In all cases where military officers and soldiers do not return to camp garrisons, arriving officials do not return to official quarters, traveling envoys do not return to relay stations, yet rashly lodge in civilian homes harming the people—provincial administrations and surveillance platforms send them away and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers and soldiers, arriving officials, and traveling envoys who lodge in civilian homes instead of camps, offices, or relay stations, harming the people, are sent away and prosecuted by the provincial administration and surveillance platform.

sentences.zh: 到任官無官舍，出私錢僦居者聽。

translations.literal: Arriving officials without official quarters who spend private money to rent lodging—permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving officials without government quarters may rent lodging with private funds.

sentences.zh: 諸造謀以已賣田宅，誣買主占奪，脅取錢物者，計贓論罪，仍紅泥粉壁書過於門。

translations.literal: In all cases of plotting to use already-sold fields and houses to falsely accuse the buyer of seizure, extorting money and goods—sentence according to stolen goods; still smear red mud on the wall and write the offense at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Those who scheme with already-sold property to falsely accuse the buyer of seizure and extort money are sentenced according to the amount taken; the offense is written on the gate in red.

sentences.zh: 諸婚田訴訟，必於本年結絕，已經務停而不結絕者，從廉訪司及本管上司，正官吏之罪。

translations.literal: In all cases of marriage-field litigation, must be concluded within the current year; those already suspended yet not concluded—follow surveillance commission and supervising superior to punish the chief official and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage and land suits must be concluded within the year; those suspended without conclusion are referred to the surveillance commission and superior authority to punish the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 累經務停，而不結絕者，即與歸結，不在務停之限，違者罪亦如之。

translations.literal: Those repeatedly suspended yet not concluded—immediately conclude and return; not within suspension limits; violators punished likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Cases repeatedly suspended without conclusion are immediately closed; further suspension is not permitted; violators are punished likewise.

sentences.zh: 其所爭田內租入，納稅之外，並從有司收貯，斷後隨田給付。

translations.literal: Rent from the disputed fields within, beyond tax paid, all follow offices to store; after judgment follow the fields and deliver.
translations.idiomatic: Rent from the disputed land, beyond tax already paid, is held by the proper offices and delivered with the land after judgment.

sentences.zh: 諸以女子典雇於人，及典雇人之子女者，並禁止之。

translations.literal: In all cases of pawning or hiring out girls to others, and hiring out others' sons and daughters—all prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Pawning girls to others or hiring out others' sons and daughters are both forbidden.

sentences.zh: 若已典雇，願以婚嫁之禮為妻妾者，聽。

translations.literal: If already pawned or hired and willing to take as wife or concubine by marriage rites—permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If already pawned or hired, taking the person as wife or concubine by proper marriage rites is permitted.

sentences.zh: 諸受錢典雇妻妾者，禁。

translations.literal: In all cases of receiving money to pawn or hire wives and concubines—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving money to pawn or hire out wives and concubines is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其夫婦同雇而不相離者，聽。

translations.literal: Husband and wife hired together and not separated—permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife hired together without separation is permitted.

sentences.zh: 諸受財嫁賣妻妾及過房弟妹者，禁。

translations.literal: In all cases of receiving wealth to marry off or sell wives and concubines and adopted younger siblings—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving payment to marry off or sell wives, concubines, or adopted younger siblings is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸乞養過房男女者，聽；

translations.literal: In all cases of begging to adopt and take in sons and daughters—permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Begging to adopt sons and daughters is permitted;

sentences.zh: 轉賣為奴婢者，禁之。

translations.literal: Reselling as slave servants—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Reselling them as bond servants is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 奴婢過房良民者，禁之。

translations.literal: Slave servants adopted into commoner households—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting bond servants into commoner households is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸守宰抑取部民男女為奴婢者，杖七十七，期年後降二等雜職敘。

translations.literal: In all cases where magistrates rashly seize subjects' sons and daughters as slave servants—seventy-seven strokes; after one year demoted two grades in miscellaneous service appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who seize subjects' sons or daughters as bond servants receive seventy-seven strokes and, after one year, are demoted two grades in miscellaneous appointments.

sentences.zh: 諸妄認良人為奴，非理殘虐者，杖八十七，有官者罷之。

translations.literal: In all cases of rashly claiming commoners as slaves and tormenting them without principle—eighty-seven strokes; those with office are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who falsely claim commoners as slaves and abuse them receive eighty-seven strokes; officials are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸訴良得實，給據居住，候元籍親屬收領，無親屬者聽令自便。

translations.literal: In all cases of suing as commoner and obtaining truth, issue certificate to reside; await original-register kin to receive; those without kin are permitted to go as they will.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sue successfully to prove commoner status receive a certificate to reside; they await kin from the original register to receive them; those without kin may go as they please.

sentences.zh: 諸奴婢背主在逃，杖七十七。

translations.literal: In all cases of slave servants fleeing their master—seventy-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Bond servants who flee their master receive seventy-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 諸男女議婚，有以指腹割衿為定者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases where men and women betroth using finger-pointing or cutting robe as pledge—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothal by pointing at the womb or cutting robe scraps as pledge is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸嫁娶之家，飲食宴好，求足成禮，以華侈相尚，暮夜不休者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of marrying households, food, drink, feasts, seeking sufficiency to complete rites, competing in luxury through the night without cease—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Wedding feasts that pursue extravagance to complete the rites and vie in luxury through the night are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸男女婚姻，媒氏違例多索聘財，及多取媒利者，諭眾決譴。

translations.literal: In all cases of men and women marrying, matchmakers violating rules by demanding much betrothal wealth and taking much matchmaker profit—admonish publicly and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Matchmakers who violate rules by demanding excessive betrothal payments or taking excessive fees are publicly admonished and punished.

sentences.zh: 諸女子已許嫁而未成婚，其夫家犯叛逆，應沒入者，若其夫為盜及犯流遠者，皆聽改嫁。

translations.literal: In all cases of girls already betrothed yet not married, if the groom's household commits rebellion and should be confiscated, or if the groom is a robber or suffers distant exile—all permitted to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: A girl betrothed but not yet married may remarry if the groom's household is subject to confiscation for rebellion, or if the groom is a robber or exiled to distant punishment.

sentences.zh: 已成婚有子，其夫雖為盜受罪，勿改嫁。

translations.literal: Already married with children; though the husband is robber and suffers punishment—do not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: If already married with children, the wife may not remarry even if the husband is convicted as a robber.

sentences.zh: 諸男女既定婚，其女犯奸事覺，夫家欲棄，則追還聘財，不棄則減半成婚。

translations.literal: In all cases where men and women are betrothed and the girl's adultery is discovered, if the groom's household wishes to abandon—return betrothal wealth; if not abandoning—reduce by half and complete marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Where betrothed and the girl's adultery is discovered, if the groom's family wishes to withdraw, betrothal payments are returned; if not, marriage proceeds at half the betrothal price.

sentences.zh: 若夫家輒詭以風聞奸事，恐脅成親者，笞五十七，離之。

translations.literal: If the groom's household rashly uses rumored adultery to threaten and force marriage—fifty-seven strokes; divorce.
translations.idiomatic: If the groom's family falsely claims adultery by rumor to coerce marriage—fifty-seven strokes and divorce.

sentences.zh: 諸遭父母喪，忘哀拜靈成婚者，杖八十七，離之，有官者罷之，仍沒其聘財，婦人不坐。

translations.literal: In all cases of suffering parents' mourning yet forgetting grief, bowing at the spirit tablet and completing marriage—eighty-seven strokes, divorce; those with office dismissed; still confiscate betrothal wealth; the woman not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Marrying during parents' mourning without proper grief—eighty-seven strokes and divorce; officials are dismissed; betrothal wealth is confiscated; the woman is not punished.

sentences.zh: 諸服內定婚，各減服內成親罪二等，仍離之，聘財沒官。

translations.literal: In all cases of betrothal within mourning, each reduces the crime of marrying within mourning by two grades; still divorce; betrothal wealth confiscated to government.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothal during mourning reduces the penalty for marrying during mourning by two grades; divorce still applies; betrothal wealth is confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸有女許嫁，已報書及有私約，或已受聘財而輒悔者，笞三十七；

translations.literal: In all cases where a daughter is promised in marriage, already reported in writing or with private agreement, or already received betrothal wealth yet rashly regrets—thirty-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: Where a daughter is promised, with written notice, private agreement, or betrothal received, rash regret—thirty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 更許他人者，笞四十七；

translations.literal: Promising to another—forty-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: Promising her to another—forty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 已成婚者，五十七；

translations.literal: Already married—fifty-seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: If already married to another—fifty-seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 後娶知情者，減一等，女歸前夫。

translations.literal: The later husband if knowing—reduced one grade; the woman returns to former husband.
translations.idiomatic: A later husband who knew the prior betrothal is punished one grade lighter; the woman returns to the first husband.

sentences.zh: 男家悔者，不坐，不追聘財，五年無故不娶者，有司給據改嫁。

translations.literal: If the groom's household regrets—not punished, betrothal wealth not pursued; five years without cause not marrying—the proper offices issue certificate for remarriage.
translations.idiomatic: If the groom's family withdraws, they are not punished and betrothal wealth is not reclaimed; if the groom fails to marry without cause for five years, the proper offices issue a certificate permitting remarriage.

sentences.zh: 諸有女納婿，復逐婿，納他人為婿者，杖六十七。

translations.literal: In all cases where a daughter takes a son-in-law, then drives the son-in-law away and takes another as son-in-law—sixty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a son-in-law into the household, then expelling him and taking another—sixty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 後婿同其罪，女歸前夫，聘財沒官。

translations.literal: The later son-in-law shares the crime; the woman returns to former husband; betrothal wealth confiscated to government.
translations.idiomatic: The later son-in-law shares the penalty; the woman returns to the first husband; betrothal wealth is confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸職官娶娼為妻者，笞五十七，解職，離之。

translations.literal: In all cases of officials marrying courtesans as wives—fifty-seven strokes, removed from office, divorce.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who marry courtesans as wives receive fifty-seven strokes, are removed from office, and must divorce.

sentences.zh: 諸有妻妾復娶妻妾者，笞四十七，離之。

translations.literal: In all cases of having wife and concubines yet again marrying wife and concubines—forty-seven strokes, divorce.
translations.idiomatic: Those with wives and concubines who marry additional wives or concubines receive forty-seven strokes and must divorce.

sentences.zh: 在官者，解職記過，不追聘財。

translations.literal: Those in office—removed and recorded demerit; betrothal wealth not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are removed and demerit recorded; betrothal wealth is not reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 諸先通奸被斷，復娶以為妻妾者，雖有所生男女，猶離之。

translations.literal: In all cases of prior adultery already judged, again marrying as wife or concubine—even with children born, still divorce.
translations.idiomatic: Marrying as wife or concubine one previously convicted of adultery with—even if children were born—still requires divorce.

sentences.zh: 諸轉嫁已歸未成婚男婦者，杖六十七，婦歸宗，聘財沒官。

translations.literal: In all cases of remarrying a woman already returned but not yet married—sixty-seven strokes; the woman returns to her clan; betrothal wealth confiscated to government.
translations.idiomatic: Remarrying a woman who has returned to her clan but is not yet wed again—sixty-seven strokes; she returns to her clan; betrothal wealth is confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸受財以妻轉嫁者，杖六十七，追還聘財；

translations.literal: In all cases of receiving wealth to have one's wife remarried—sixty-seven strokes; pursue and return betrothal wealth;
translations.idiomatic: Receiving payment to have one's wife remarried—sixty-seven strokes; betrothal wealth is recovered;

sentences.zh: 娶者不知情，不坐，婦人歸宗。

translations.literal: The taker if not knowing—not punished; the woman returns to her clan.
translations.idiomatic: A husband who did not know is not punished; the woman returns to her clan.

sentences.zh: 諸以書幣娶人女為妾，復受財轉嫁他人者，笞五十七，聘財沒官，妾歸宗，有官者罷之。

translations.literal: In all cases of taking another's daughter as concubine by letter and gifts, again receiving wealth and remarrying her to another—fifty-seven strokes; betrothal wealth confiscated to government; concubine returns to clan; those with office dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Taking another's daughter as concubine by formal gifts, then receiving payment to marry her to someone else—fifty-seven strokes; betrothal wealth confiscated; the concubine returns to her clan; officials are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸僧道悖教娶妻者，杖六十七，離之，僧道還俗為民，聘財沒官。

translations.literal: In all cases of monks and Taoists violating teaching to take wives—sixty-seven strokes, divorce; monks and Taoists return to lay life as commoners; betrothal wealth confiscated to government.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Taoists who marry in violation of their vows receive sixty-seven strokes and must divorce; they return to lay life; betrothal wealth is confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸典賣佃戶者，禁。

translations.literal: In all cases of pawning or selling tenant households—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Pawning or selling tenant households is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 佃戶嫁娶，從其父母。

translations.literal: Tenant households marrying—follow their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Tenant households' marriages follow their parents' authority.

sentences.zh: 諸兄收弟婦者，杖一百七，婦九十七，離之。

translations.literal: In all cases of elder brother taking younger brother's wife—one hundred seven strokes; the woman ninety-seven; divorce.
translations.idiomatic: An elder brother who takes his younger brother's wife receives one hundred seven strokes; the woman ninety-seven; divorce is required.

sentences.zh: 雖出首，仍坐。

translations.literal: Though turning oneself in—still punished.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one surrenders voluntarily, the penalty still applies.

sentences.zh: 主婚笞五十七，行媒三十七。

translations.literal: The marriage arranger—fifty-seven strokes; the go-between—thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The marriage arranger receives fifty-seven strokes; the go-between thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諸居父母喪，奸收庶母者，各杖一百七，離之，有官者除名。

translations.literal: In all cases of dwelling in parents' mourning, committing adultery and taking a concubine mother—each one hundred seven strokes, divorce; those with office removed from roster.
translations.idiomatic: During parents' mourning, committing adultery with or taking a father's concubine (concubine-mother)—each receives one hundred seven strokes and divorce; officials are struck from the roster.

sentences.zh: 諸漢人、南人，父沒子收其庶母，兄沒弟收其嫂者，禁之。

translations.literal: In all cases of Han and southern people, father dead son taking his concubine mother, elder brother dead younger brother taking his sister-in-law—forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han and southern subjects, a son taking his father's concubine after the father's death, or a younger brother taking his elder brother's widow, is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸姑表兄弟嫂叔不相收，收者以奸論。

translations.literal: In all cases of paternal-cousin brother's wife and paternal-cousin uncle not taking each other—if taken, sentenced as adultery.
translations.idiomatic: Among cross-cousins, a man must not take his cousin's wife in levirate; if he does, it is sentenced as adultery.

sentences.zh: 諸奴收主妻者，以奸論；

translations.literal: In all cases of slaves taking the master's wife—sentenced as adultery;
translations.idiomatic: A slave who takes his master's wife is sentenced as adultery;

sentences.zh: 強收主女者，處死。

translations.literal: Forcibly taking the master's daughter—executed.
translations.idiomatic: Forcibly taking the master's daughter is punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 諸為子輒以亡父之妾與人，人輒受而私之，與者杖七十七，受者笞五十七。

translations.literal: In all cases of sons rashly giving the deceased father's concubine to another, another rashly receiving and keeping privately—giver seventy-seven strokes, receiver fifty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Sons who give away a deceased father's concubine, and those who privately accept her— the giver receives seventy-seven strokes, the receiver fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諸受財強嫁所監臨妻，以枉法論，杖七十七，除名，追財沒官，妻還前夫。

translations.literal: In all cases of receiving wealth to forcibly marry the wife of one under supervision—sentenced for bending the law, seventy-seven strokes, removed from roster, pursue wealth confiscated to government; wife returns to former husband.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving payment to forcibly marry the wife of a subordinate under one's supervision is sentenced as bending the law: seventy-seven strokes, removal from the roster, payment confiscated, and the wife returned to her former husband.

sentences.zh: 諸良家女願與人奴為婚者，即為奴婢。

translations.literal: In all cases where a freeborn woman willingly marries another person's slave, she immediately becomes a bondwoman.
translations.idiomatic: A freeborn woman who willingly marries another person's slave immediately becomes a bondwoman.

sentences.zh: 娶良家女為妻，以為奴婢賣之者，即改正為良，賣主買主同罪，價沒官。

translations.literal: One who takes a freeborn woman as wife and then treats and sells her as a bondwoman—she is immediately restored to free status; seller and buyer share the same crime; the price is confiscated for the state.
translations.idiomatic: A man who marries a freeborn woman and then sells her as a bondwoman must restore her to free status; seller and buyer are punished alike, and the price is confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸以童養未成婚男婦轉配其奴者，笞五十七，婦歸宗，不追聘財。

translations.literal: In all cases where one transfers a child-betrothed but unmarried couple to marry a slave, he receives fifty-seven strokes of the rod; the woman returns to her lineage; betrothal wealth is not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Transferring a child-betrothed couple to marry a slave brings fifty-seven strokes; the woman returns to her family and betrothal gifts are not recovered.

sentences.zh: 諸逃奴有女，嫁為良人妻，已有男女，而本主覺察者，追其聘財歸本主，婦人不離。

translations.literal: In all cases where a fugitive slave has a daughter who marries a free man as wife and already has children, and the original master discovers it, betrothal wealth is pursued and returned to the original master; the woman is not separated.
translations.idiomatic: When a fugitive slave's daughter has married a free man and borne children, and the original master discovers it, betrothal gifts are recovered for the master; the woman is not separated from her husband.

sentences.zh: 諸棄妻，已歸宗改嫁者，從其後夫。

translations.literal: In all cases of a discarded wife who has returned to her lineage and remarried, she follows her later husband.
translations.idiomatic: A discarded wife who has returned home and remarried follows her new husband.

sentences.zh: 諸棄妻改嫁，後夫亡，復納以為妻者，離之。

translations.literal: In all cases where a discarded wife remarries, her later husband dies, and she is taken back as wife again, they are separated.
translations.idiomatic: A discarded wife who remarried, whose second husband died, and who is taken back by her first husband must be divorced.

sentences.zh: 諸夫婦不相睦，賣休買休者禁之，違者罪之，和離者不坐。

translations.literal: In all cases where husband and wife are not harmonious, selling divorce or buying divorce is prohibited; violators are punished; mutually agreed separation is not punished.
translations.idiomatic: When husband and wife are estranged, buying or selling divorce is forbidden and violators are punished; mutually agreed separation is not an offense.

sentences.zh: 諸出妻妾，須約以書契，聽其改嫁。

translations.literal: In all cases of dismissing a wife or concubine, a written contract must be made, and she is permitted to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissing a wife or concubine requires a written contract, after which she may remarry.

sentences.zh: 以手模為征者，禁之。

translations.literal: Using a handprint as proof is prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Using a handprint alone as proof of agreement is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 諸婦人背夫、棄舅姑出家為尼者，杖六十七，還其夫。

translations.literal: In all cases where a woman abandons her husband and parents-in-law to become a nun, she receives sixty-seven strokes of the staff and is returned to her husband.
translations.idiomatic: A woman who abandons her husband and parents-in-law to become a nun receives sixty-seven strokes and is returned to her husband.

sentences.zh: 諸賣買良人為倡，賣主買主同罪，婦還為良，價錢半沒官，半付告者。

translations.literal: In all cases of buying and selling a free person as a courtesan, seller and buyer share the same crime; the woman is restored to free status; half the price is confiscated for the state and half given to the informant.
translations.idiomatic: Buying or selling a free person as a courtesan: seller and buyer are punished alike; the woman is freed; half the price goes to the state and half to the informant.

sentences.zh: 或婦人自陳，或因事發覺，全沒入之。

translations.literal: If the woman confesses herself, or the matter is discovered through an incident, the entire price is confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: If the woman confesses or the matter comes to light, the entire price is confiscated.

sentences.zh: 良家婦犯奸，為夫所棄，或倡優親屬，願為倡者聽。

translations.literal: A freeborn woman who commits adultery and is discarded by her husband, or relatives of entertainers who wish to become courtesans, are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: A freeborn adulteress discarded by her husband, or relatives of entertainers who wish to become courtesans, may do so.

sentences.zh: 諸倡女孕，勒令墮胎者，犯人坐罪，倡放為良。

translations.literal: In all cases where a courtesan is pregnant and is forced to abort, the offender is punished; the courtesan is released to free status.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing a pregnant courtesan to abort is punishable; the courtesan is freed.

sentences.zh: 諸勒妻妾為倡者，杖八十七。

translations.literal: In all cases where one forces a wife or concubine to become a courtesan, he receives eighty-seven strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing a wife or concubine into prostitution brings eighty-seven strokes.

sentences.zh: 以乞養良家女，為人歌舞，給宴樂，及勒為倡者，杖七十七，婦人並歸宗。

translations.literal: One who takes in a freeborn girl to sing and dance for others' banquets and entertainment, or forces her to become a courtesan, receives seventy-seven strokes of the staff; the woman is returned to her lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Taking in a freeborn girl for singing, dancing, or banquets, or forcing her into prostitution, brings seventy-seven strokes; the woman returns to her family.

sentences.zh: 勒奴婢為倡者，笞四十七，婦人放從良。

translations.literal: One who forces a bondwoman to become a courtesan receives forty-seven strokes of the rod; the woman is released to free status.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing a bondwoman into prostitution brings forty-seven strokes; she is freed.

sentences.zh: 諸受財縱妻妾為倡者，本夫與奸婦奸夫各杖八十七，離之。

translations.literal: In all cases where one accepts payment and allows a wife or concubine to become a courtesan, the husband and the adulterous woman and adulterous man each receive eighty-seven strokes of the staff; they are separated.
translations.idiomatic: A husband who takes payment and allows his wife or concubine to prostitute herself, together with her lover, each receive eighty-seven strokes and must divorce.

sentences.zh: 其妻妾隨時自首者，不坐；

translations.literal: If the wife or concubine confesses promptly, she is not punished;
translations.idiomatic: A wife or concubine who confesses promptly is not punished;

sentences.zh: 若日月已久才自首者，勿聽。

translations.literal: if after many days and months she confesses, her confession is not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: if she confesses only after a long delay, her confession is not accepted.
